Discovering novel intent categories from user inputs is a critical component of dialogue systems, yet current methods typically depend on large volumes of labeled data for each newly introduced category, which is often costly and difficult to obtain. This study introduces a new approach for discovering and classifying user intents that utilizes only a small number of labeled examples. Specifically, we employ a pre-trained language model to generate high-quality pseudo-labels for unannotated conversations, followed by the application of contrastive learning to enhance the model's sensitivity to subtle variations in input. Our experiments, conducted on the newly developed SuperNaturaliCi dataset, demonstrate that this method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in scenarios with limited data.

The classical universal bundle functor $W: sGrp \rightarrow sTop$, which maps a simplicial group to a corresponding simplicial topological space, was originally defined by Kan and has since been extensively analyzed by various authors. This paper establishes the uniqueness of $W$ within the category of simplicial functors originating from simplicial groups and landing in simplicial topological spaces, subject to constraints imposed by stalks. Furthermore, it provides a characterization of those specific topological spaces that form part of the functor's image.

"This paper presents an explicit upper limit on the count of subgroups within any finite group, defined by the group's order and its rank. For groups with rank at most two, precise bounds are established, including exact formulas for the number of cyclic subgroups in these cases."

This study offers a novel geometric derivation of the ABS H2 equation, establishing its connection to discrete self-dual Lorentzian metrics on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. We introduce a specific class of discrete metrics characterized by alternating signatures across quadrants of the integer lattice and demonstrate that these quadrants' metric components are governed by quadruply discrete linear equations. The proof reveals that the ABS H2 equation emerges as the sole solution compatible with both self-duality and a particular quadrantal signature pattern.

Visual Relationship Detection (VRD) aims to identify interactions between objects in an image, such as "a cup sitting on a table." While recent advancements have yielded strong performance on the standard VRD benchmark, these results are largely driven by an imbalanced dataset that favors the detection of rare relationships. This study introduces a new synthetic dataset designed to challenge the detection of uncommon false positives. We evaluate current state-of-the-art models against this benchmark, revealing significant performance gaps. To address these limitations, we propose a novel method leveraging contrastive learning and a synthetic challenge to improve robustness. Finally, we demonstrate that our model maintains strong efficacy on the standard benchmark while successfully mitigating false detections in scenarios involving rare relationships.

In this study, we introduce a protocol utilizing weak measurement to partially and predictably disentangle initially separable states. By applying this method, we can adjust the degree of entanglement in quantum states through weak measurement, allowing for the precise and controlled reduction of entanglement. We further establish a quantum correlation cost associated with weak measurement, representing the minimum amount of correlation disrupted when the measurement is performed. This metric enables an analysis of the relationship between the measurement strength and the resulting loss of correlations. Our findings demonstrate that both the weak-value amplification process and the optimal control strategy for quantum state preparation can be effectively modeled using this correlation cost framework.

This work introduces an AnEnd-to-End deep learning framework designed to construct a social relationship graph from textual data. The model comprises two primary components: a social attribute extractor that generates relationship-specific features like titles and sentiment, and a social link predictor that utilizes these attributes to form connections between entities. The feature extraction module employs a hybrid architecture combining bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) networks with a transformer encoder, leveraging textual context to produce precise social attributes. The link prediction module then applies a self-attention mechanism to the extracted features, determining whether a specific social link exists between entity pairs. Evaluated against the CoSoRe dataset, the proposed method achieved a macro F1 score of 0.605, surpassing existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have become the standard for many computer vision tasks, yet their fixed architecture and lack of flexibility in feature extraction often limit performance. This work introduces a new approach using Message Passing Networks (MPNs) on dynamic graphs to address visual recognition problems. By modeling image features as nodes within a graph, this method allows for more flexible learning compared to CNNs. We specifically propose a novel architecture capable of learning both node attributes and the graph structure itself directly from data. Extensive testing across various visual recognition benchmarks demonstrates that this structure significantly boosts performance, achieving state-of-the-art results in several key tasks.

Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) is a fundamental operation in digital signal processing that can be realized with significantly lower hardware complexity than the standard approach if an optimal architecture is selected. This study introduces a new method for generating such optimal designs by employing the Shortest Vector Lattice (SVL) algorithm to determine the minimal set of coefficients required for MCM implementation using a 3-to-1 multiplier. This approach is extended to scenarios involving a P-constant multiplication with P > 3 by integrating an MCM co-design methodology with the SVL technique. The experimental results demonstrate that these proposed techniques outperform current state-of-the-art methods in terms of both the minimal hardware cost and the total computational effort required.

Quantum machine learning (QML) represents a rapidly emerging field within quantum computing, with quantum neural networks (QNNs) serving as a pivotal component. This article provides a comprehensive overview of the fundamental principles, potential applications, and the significant challenges associated with QNNs. We begin by defining the architecture and operational mechanisms of these networks, followed by an examination of their use cases in pattern recognition and data classification. The discussion also highlights current obstacles, including noise inherent in present quantum hardware, scalability issues, and the lack of suitable theoretical frameworks for hyperparameter optimization. Finally, we outline promising future research trajectories aimed at overcoming these barriers and advancing the field toward practical, real-world implementation.

Radiofrequency (RF) accelerator systems serve as the essential backbone for particle physics research, enabling the generation of high-energy particle beams. This document provides a comprehensive overview of current RF accelerator technology development efforts, with a specific emphasis on advancements in superconducting RF (SRF) cavities and normal-conducting RF (NRCAF) systems. It examines the progress and challenges associated with these technologies as they pertain to the proposed International Muon Collider and the proposed CLICdee concept. Furthermore, the report outlines the technology development requirements for RF systems required by various proposed high-energy physics colliders and astrophysics drivers.

The LHC's findings have revitalized the search for physics beyond the Standard Model, positioning the muon collider as an ideal instrument to address these inquiries. This paper outlines the project's history, current status, and future trajectory while examining the technical obstacles involved in achieving a clean muon collider.

This study examines the dispersion relations of linearized perturbations within a viscous relativistic fluid, governed by a conformally invariant, causal, and stable hydrodynamic framework. This framework adheres to the principles of relativistic invariance and maintains compliance with the entropy production requirement. By employing a Green-Kubo formula, the paper establishes the permissible bounds for transport coefficients, ensuring they support a stable and causal evolution of perturbations. Consequently, the resulting dispersion relations delineate the conditions under which stable and causal propagation occurs for both scalar and sound waves.

We investigate the radio photon backgrounds generated by primordial black holes (PBHs) within the standard cosmological model. Our analysis indicates that a fraction of the observed radio sky can be attributed to this radiation, provided the PBH mass distribution is concentrated in the $10^{15}$ to $10^{17}$ kg range.

This study introduces the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a processor architecture designed to execute computations confidentially using Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE). The architecture employs a five-stage pipeline and incorporates specialized co-processants to accelerate operations on FHE ciphertexts. We have implemented this platform on the FPGA, utilizing the CKKS scheme for approximate arithmetic. Performance evaluations conducted on the VSP demonstrate execution times of 1.1 seconds for the secure Dijkstra algorithm and 1.9 seconds for the Paillier encryption of the BERT machine learning model.

The computational difficulty of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) varies significantly based on their domain size and structure; specifically, problems with bounded domain sizes are typically solvable in polynomial time when sparse, whereas those with unbounded domains often remain NP-hard even under sparsity constraints. This paper addresses general-valued CSPs over an infinite, ordered domain, establishing that for any instance with bounded relative and absolute sparsity constraints, either a polynomial-time algorithm producing a solution within a factor of $1-\epsilon$ of the optimum (for any $\epsilon > 0$) exists, or the problem is coNP-complete.

Pretrained language models have significantly advanced Natural Language Processing, yet their utility in syntactic parsing remains limited. This paper introduces a new approach to unsupervised and few-shot dependency parsing that leverages the capabilities of these models. We demonstrate that the self-attention mechanisms within the architecture implicitly encode structural syntax, allowing our method to identify dependencies effectively even with minimal or no labeled data. Extensive experiments show that this approach surpasses strong baselines in unsupervised environments and achieves state-of-the-art results for dependency parsing on multiple languages without any training annotations. Furthermore, our method outperforms existing techniques in few-shot scenarios, successfully acquiring parsing abilities for previously unseen languages using just twenty annotated sentences.

High-dimensional hyperspectral images (HSIs) offer a rich array of spectral and spatial details, making them highly effective for semantic segmentation. This study introduces a novel, cost-efficient, weakly-supervised framework designed to generate semantic labels for driving scenes using HSI data. We hypothesize that the extensive spectral-spatial information within these images enables the precise distinction between diverse objects, even in the absence of extensive annotation. To validate this, we developed a new architecture based on a spectral-spatial fusion mechanism that performs robust segmentation. Furthermore, we propose a two-stage training process to optimize the model's parameters. Extensive experiments conducted on the driving dataset using both synthetic and real-world HSI confirm that our method surpasses current state-of-the-art techniques.

Recent observations by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) reveal that the atmosphere of the ultra-short-period (USP) planet WASP-187b exhibits a surprisingly high spin-orbit misalignment of 50° ± 10°. This planet orbits its host star at an extremely close distance of 0.014 AU, a proximity that typically results in tidally locked rotation. Previous studies have suggested that the planet's current spin-orbit angle results from a gradual realignment process driven by the migration of the tidal dissipation mechanism within the interior. However, our analysis of the atmospheric dynamics indicates that the observed 50° tilt is more likely caused by the rapid migration of the planet toward the star due to tidal forces, a process triggered by the engulfment of the stellar surface layers. This scenario suggests that the planet's angular momentum was reset to near zero shortly before this engulfment event. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that the observed atmospheric tilt can serve as a diagnostic tool to distinguish between models of tidal dissipation operating in rocky versus gaseous interiors.

In the RAM model with addition, we examine the constant-time computability of standard arithmetic operations. This study extends previous work by D. Coppersmith et al. [2018], who demonstrated that multiplication, division, and the floor of the square-root are all executable in constant time. We further prove that calculating the floor of the square-sum ($\lfloor\sqrt{x+y}\rfloor$) and determining bit-length ($|x|$) both occur in constant time. Conversely, we demonstrate that computing the absolute value ($|x|$) cannot be achieved in constant time.

Session-based recommendations aim to forecast future items by modeling user interactions within brief timeframes, a challenge that demands rapid convergence of deep learning architectures. This study introduces a self-supervised graph neural network (GNN) framework designed to enhance prediction accuracy by leveraging self-supervised objectives. Furthermore, we present a graph co-training strategy that employs two distinct encoders to jointly analyze both historical and future item data, thereby facilitating faster convergence. Extensive testing across three widely used datasets confirms the efficacy of our self-supervised approach and the significant improvements in both convergence speed and recommendation performance.

This study introduces group LCD (linear complementary dual) codes, defined as the linear dual of a subgroup of $G$ being an independent subspace of $G$, where $G$ represents an abelian group. We establish group LCD codes within the framework of cyclic, abelian, and permutation equivalent groups. Furthermore, we derive group-theoretic counterparts to the Hamming, Simplex, and Reed-Muller codes. The paper concludes by presenting various constructions and properties of these codes, alongside new results linking group LCD codes to classical group codes.

We establish a general framework to express invariant differential forms on moduli spaces of curves using algebraic tools. This approach, which may be of broad interest, leverages the combinatorics of compactifications of moduli spaces of curves defined by their associated stratifications into graphs. Specifically, we demonstrate that the differential forms arising in the computation of Feynman integrals for the $t$-deformation of the Losev-Manin lattice remain within a space of algebraic compactification that preserves the property of being a smooth variety.

Although object categorization relies on features such as shape and texture, it remains unclear how these distinct attributes are prioritized during the course of recognition. This study investigates that priority by training convolutional and recurrent neural networks to perform object categorization. The results indicate that in both convolutional and recurrent architectures, category-defining information emerges early, whereas feature-specific signals related to texture or shape appear later. Crucially, when equi-trained networks were manipulated to favor either shape or texture, the spatial distribution of when those attributes were encoded remained identical. These findings suggest that the temporal sequencing of shape versus texture information is intrinsic to the recurrent processing stage and is independent of the relevance of those features for the specific task.

Non-Hermitian topological phases are defined by the presence of non-trivial topology within a real space, manifesting in either line gaps or point gaps in their energy bands. While line-gap topology is tied to Hermitian symmetries, point-gap topology exists independently of them, appearing in systems lacking such protection. This study examines how correlations in an open-chain non-Hermitian spinless Fermi model affect point-gap topology. We demonstrate that, unlike isolated sites, non-zero hopping destroys the point gap when the system is in a product state. Conversely, in a general pure state, correlations induced by hopping can sustain the point gap. We find a critical region in parameter space where correlations are strong enough to restore the point gap, thereby reducing the resulting topological phase.

Recently, research has focused on developing polyphase Golay complementary arrays (PGCA), which join two distinct arrays where the sum of their autocorrelation sequences yields zero outside a single lag. This paper introduces novel methods for building PGCA using phase- and time- (or frequency-) shifted Golay complementary pairs (GCP) and phase- or time- (or frequency-) shifted Hadamard matrices. Specifically, we present three new single-element wide PGCA constructions and multiple general approaches for creating PGCA with arbitrary dimensions. Furthermore, we introduce new families of PRID sequences and Hadamard-based PGCA that surpass existing solutions in performance. Numerically, we demonstrate that the proposed solutions outperform current state-of-the-art methods in maximizing the achievable array size for a given length.

This study reports combined results from CMS and ATLAS concerning the decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson into two pairs of muons and tau leptons. The analysis examines on-shell production, where the Higgs decays via an intermediate resonance, and off-shell production, where it occurs without such an intermediate state. By comparing off-shell to on-shell production rates, the study derives the Higgs boson width, yielding $\Gamma_{\text{h}} = 12^{+10}_{-8} \text{ (stat)} \pm 5 \text{ (syst)}$ MeV. Furthermore, limits are established for anomalous couplings in the vector–boson–Higgs interaction, specifically for the $a_{\text{hvv}}$ and $b_{\text{hvv}}$ parameters.

Detecting changes in multispectral and hyperspectral imagery is a critical challenge with broad implications across the geospatial community. This work introduces a new technique for bi-temporal change detection in hyperspectral data by employing deep autoencoders. The method utilizes Convolutional Autoencoders (CAEs) to learn a low-dimensional latent representation of the input data, effectively fusing features across all spectral bands. This dimensionality reduction step significantly lowers computational complexity. Furthermore, the approach enhances robustness against domain shifts caused by varying illumination conditions and sensor characteristics. Change detection is subsequently performed on the compressed latent space to identify discrepancies between image pairs. Experimental results using two real-world hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Let $N$ be a sufficiently large integer. We demonstrate that the expected value of $\sum_{n \le N} (\tau(n) - 2)^2$ for nonsquare-free $\tau$ is at least $cN$ for some positive constant $c$. This finding extends to the case where $\tau$ is restricted to be the characteristic function of the set of squares. These findings build upon the work of Hooley and Iwaniec-Goldston, who established the result for the general case and the case where $\tau$ is the square characteristic function, respectively; however, our approach also covers the scenario where $\tau$ is the characteristic function of almost all squares (with a density approaching 1).

This study utilizes scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS) to investigate silicon-28 doped with phosphorus, focusing on the tunneling current's valley interference and spin-exchange interactions. By examining the energy dependence of the current, we observe that valley interference persists even when the tunneling states are delocalized, whereas spin-exchange interactions remain confined to the immediate vicinity of the atoms. Consequently, we propose that scanning tunneling spectroscopy serves as a viable technique for measuring the spatial extent of both phenomena.

Optimization is a fundamental mathematical technique with extensive applications across various domains. While numerous open-source libraries exist for general optimization, they typically prioritize specific domains like machine learning or lack the speed and efficiency required for rapid experimentation. Consequently, these tools are ill-suited for the early stages of developing new optimization methods. To address this gap, we introduce LibOPT, an open-source Python platform designed to facilitate the quick development, testing, and deployment of novel mathematical optimization algorithms. LibOPT offers a comprehensive suite of standard test functions, benchmarking capabilities, and a user-friendly interface for custom algorithm integration. Additionally, it includes a collection of established solvers and strategies, such as evolutionary algorithms, simulated annealing, and tabu search. By enabling the creation of tailored optimizers with minimal effort, LibOPT serves as an effective instrument for both academic research and practical industrial use.

For a connected algebraic group $G$ acting on an irreducible algebraic variety $X$, we define the value $\deg_G(X)$ as the maximal integer $d$ for which a finite collection of $d$-tuples of the form $(x_1, \dots, x_d)$ on $X$ is not invariant under the $G$-action. In this work, we examine the properties of $\deg_G(X)$ specifically when $X$ is a homogeneous space that is a complete variety or possesses a dense orbit under a unipotent subgroup.

This work examines how quantum mechanics operates within non-commutative spacetime, a framework that generalizes the concept to particles lacking a well-defined position. We analyze the implications for quantum statistics and thermodynamics, ultimately concluding that such models fail to introduce any novel or significant effects in these areas.

Synthetic single-crystalline diamond is a promising candidate for diverse applications, including quantum sensing and radiation detection, owing to its exceptional thermal conductivity, mechanical robustness, and radiation hardness. However, the development of these applications is hindered by the presence of defects, which can be mitigated through annealing. In this study, we utilized synthetic single-crystalline diamond crystals doped with boron and subjected them to gamma-ray irradiation to introduce defects, subsequently removing these defects via thermal annealing. We employed a second-harmonic transient-current technique to map the transport edges of photogeneration within the diamond's volume. Our findings demonstrate that defects can be effectively eliminated through annealing, resulting in a significant enhancement of charge transport characteristics. Specifically, the mobility-lifetime product ($\mu\tau$) improved by a factor of 100 in both the n- and p-type diamond samples.

This study introduces a novel dataset featuring annotations for 10 distinct categories of English and Arabic misogyny found on social media. We introduce a deep multi-task model designed to detect abusive mentions of women and classify them into these specific categories simultaneously. Our experimental results indicate that the proposed approach outperforms existing single-task baselines in both detection accuracy and fine-grained classification.

Reinforcement learning (RL) has proven highly effective for discovering control policies across diverse robotic scenarios. However, ensuring a learned policy's robustness against environmental uncertainties remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates probabilistic planning into the policy search process. Specifically, the method employs probabilistic models to simulate task executions, enabling the use of established model-based RL algorithms. By leveraging these planning capabilities, the system can refine policies to be more robust. Experimental results demonstrate that this framework successfully acquires robust policies for complex manipulation tasks involving contact, even when trained on data from a simulator with discrepancies relative to the physical robot.

Caching and distributed computing have emerged as essential strategies to alleviate network congestion and enhance service delivery. This paper introduces a unified coded caching framework capable of addressing both scenarios. We demonstrate that existing literature results fall under this new model, offering a novel perspective that establishes a tight lower bound on the second moment of caching memory requirements. Furthermore, we propose a universal method for constructing the second-moment optimal tradeoff curve linking caching memory usage to server storage capacity.

This paper investigates the residue cancellation process of Eisenstein series for $GL(n)$ over rational numbers, specifically within the context of general linear groups.

Ensuring collision-free operation is critical for mobile robotic arms, particularly in dynamic and unpredictable environments. This paper introduces a novel safe control framework based on control barrier functions (CBFs) to guarantee collision avoidance. The proposed CBF formulation is tailored for mobile manipulators, accounting for both the robot's arm and base configurations. CBF constraints are integrated into a model predictive control (CBC) scheme to ensure safety. Additionally, a secondary safety layer employing dependent barrier functions (DBCs) is implemented to provide redundant protection against potential CBF control failures. Simulation results are provided to validate the efficacy of the entire framework.

Natural language processing (NLP) encompasses a range of tasks, including summarization, which aims to generate concise texts that encapsulate the original meaning. This study introduces an extractive method for achieving that goal through graph analysis. We represent words as nodes and their co-occurrences within a text as edges, subsequently applying both centrality and closeness metrics to identify and select the most significant terms. The resulting set of words is then chosen to form the summary.

This study examines a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) confined within an optical double-well system, where the coupling between the two modes exhibits nonlinearity. We demonstrate that, by adjusting the BEC's atomic scattering length via Feshbach resonance, one can realize essential nonlinear quantum logic gates operating on the quantum information stored within the condensate.

This paper establishes new theorems concerning the non-degenerate case, proving the uniqueness of meromorphic mappings where the source is a complete K\"{a}hler manifold and the target is a projective projective variety.

This work introduces a new algorithm for determining the nondegenerate variety arising from a parametric polynomial system, where the nondegenerate variety represents the closure of the nondegenerate points. We also present an algorithm for calculating the nondegenerate tangent cone at a nondegenerate point on this variety, utilizing the nondegenerate structure. Our algorithm is signature-based and functions by iteratively performing characteristic polynomial computations on elimination matrices derived from the input system, followed by the computation of modular solutions for each signature. A central component of the algorithm is the derivation of a normal form for rational sign-invariant expressions involving the parameters. Experimental evaluations were conducted on both randomly generated systems and several examples from mathematical literature.

This study reports on a low-momentum direct photon analysis from Cu+Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV, utilizing data from the PHENIX experiment at RHIC. The analysis examines transverse photon momentum spectra across centralities ranging from 10% to 90% and across rapidity intervals of $y=0$ and $|y|>3.8$. The measured spectra are contrasted with predictions from HIJING, PHJET, and PYTHIA Monte Carlo simulations, as well as with estimates derived from a superposition of thermal radiation and hadron-cyclotron decay models.

Tur\'an's Tetrahedron Problem seeks to identify the maximum number of edges in a complete weighted graph oriented on a tetrahedron such that every directed cycle has a total weight strictly greater than zero. Using the concept of oriented matroids, we establish that this maximum is $4n + 2$ for any weighting within the interior of the first octant. This result extends to all non-negative interior points on the octohedron's faces, provided the $\ell_1$-norm is used.

Anti-aliasing is a critical component of line rendering in vector map display systems. This study introduces a highly efficient, spatially localized anti-aliasing approach specifically designed for line intersections. The method achieves this by applying simple one-dimensional anti-aliasing filters to individual pixel rows and columns surrounding the feature. It maintains exceptional performance with a time complexity of O(n), where n represents the number of pixels within the feature of interest. The approach is straightforward to implement and integrates seamlessly with standard rasterization pipelines.

This study introduces a new quasi-interpolation operator utilizing radial basis functions (RBFs) with a transcendental quadratic form. The proposed operator demonstrates superior preservation properties regarding shapes, offering distinct advantages over standard multiquadric RBF quasi-interpolators. Additionally, the paper presents numerical experiments to validate the method's efficacy and accuracy.

Pulsar halos represent a hypothesized component of the interstellar medium, consisting of radiation generated by cosmic rays (both electrons and hadrons) emanating from nearby pulsars. These emissions are expected to be detectable in gamma-ray wavelengths, extending across kiloparsec scales. This overview examines the physical mechanisms governing the formation of such halos, reviews current observational data, and outlines the significant observational challenges involved in their detection.

Adverse weather conditions frequently disrupt transportation networks, causing traffic congestion and accidents, while simultaneously increasing the risk of collisions. To mitigate these issues, automated weather classification systems are increasingly vital for intelligent transport management. This study introduces a novel, publicly available dataset featuring 10 distinct categories of weather surveillance footage. To ensure fair benchmarking, we released the dataset along with randomly selected frame labels, preventing any prior knowledge of the ground truth. We also implemented a data augmentation strategy to bolster the robustness of our models. Following an extensive evaluation of various Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), we identified the most effective architecture for this task. The complete dataset and source code are publicly accessible via GitHub.

This study examines how scientific evidence, institutional frameworks, and public opinion regarding climate change intersect with social norms, specifically focusing on the economic implications of these interactions. It begins by outlining the empirical science behind climate change and the roles of key international and domestic institutions, followed by a review of public attitudes and the nature of prevailing social norms on the subject. The core of the paper analyzes the relationships among these three elements—science, institutions, and public opinion—and the social norms they shape, while exploring the economic factors driving public sentiment and the consequences of normative shifts. Ultimately, the text proposes strategies to enhance the efficacy of climate policies by fostering more constructive dynamics between scientific data, institutional actions, and societal standards.

This paper introduces a data-driven method for predicting and controlling the soft dynamics of multi-fingered grippers, utilizing the infinite-dimensional Koopman operator to create a linearized model of the soft system. This modeling framework is updated online using real-time sensor data, enabling the gripper's motion to be planned and executed by solving an optimization-based model predictive controller. The validity of this approach is confirmed through experimental results using both a single soft finger and a two-finger configuration.

Optimization techniques grounded in information geometry have proven highly effective for training deep neural networks, largely due to their theoretical ability to interpret the descent direction as the steepest slope within the manifold of model parameters. This paper introduces a novel, natural gradient-inspired descent method that offers generalized flexibility.

We report the discovery of a new, high-redshift radio source, J2102+6015, at z = 4.575, identified through observations from the VLA, ATCA, ATLAS, and 2MASS. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related fatalities globally. Although advancements in imaging, surgical techniques, and therapeutic options have improved patient outcomes, the 5-year survival rate has seen little change over the last three decades. This study introduces a deep multimodal framework designed to predict the overall survival of NSCLC patients by integrating radiological data from CT scans and genomic data derived from RNA sequencing. Our model utilizes a ResNet architecture for processing radiological features and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for processing sequencing features, with both modalities combined at the final layer. Experimental results indicate that this proposed approach outperforms existing methods, achieving a concordance index of 0.752.

Representing states is essential in reinforcement learning, yet integrating natural language poses significant challenges due to its unstructured and variable nature. This paper examines various natural language state abstraction strategies for Reinforcement Learning, categorizing them into direct encoding, metadata extraction, and semantic abstractions. We further evaluate these methods across multiple dimensions, including data volume, computational resources, and performance, ultimately offering insights and recommendations for future research.

We describe a novel machine learning strategy for deriving the density power spectrum directly from individual quasar spectra. This method involves training a neural network to predict the quasar spectra's Fourier coefficients, with the model's input consisting of the Fourier coefficients of the spectra's squared values. We demonstrate that this model effectively recovers the density power spectrum, with the amplitude scaled by a constant factor. We suggest that this technique can be applied to future large-scale spectroscopic surveys to estimate the density power spectrum.

This paper investigates the Lie algebra $\mathcal D$ of differential operators on a polynomial ring $R = \mathbb C[x]$. We demonstrate that every finite-dimensional free module over this algebra admits a finite-length composition series, with the factors being semi-simple and isomorphic to $R$ as an $\mathcal D$-module via a specific action. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between the submodules of $R$ of codimension one and the algebraic curves in the complex plane. The analysis extends to higher dimensions, where $\mathcal D$ represents the differential operators on a polynomial ring in $n$ variables. In this generalized setting, we prove that the composition factors of any finite-dimensional free $\mathcal D$-module are isomorphic to a module $R_\lambda$, where the action of $x_i$ is defined by $\partial_{x_i}$ and the operator $\partial_{\partial_{x_i}}$ is modified by a constant shift $\lambda_i \in \mathbb C$. Finally, we establish that the higher homology groups of the Lie algebra $\mathcal D$ vanish.

This study presents an end-to-end system for analyzing Twitter sentiment, utilizing a recurrency neural network to capture the sequential dependencies inherent in natural language. The research evaluates the system's performance on the well-known benchmark dataset, 41 million tweets from the 2013 Twitter Sentiment Competition, which were collected and annotated by the Sentiment Analysis Group at Cornell University. The dataset comprises English tweets from 2013 paired with sentiment labels (positive, negative, or neutral). The proposed system achieved a weighted F1 score of 0.8611, placing it in the top 10% of submissions on the competition leaderboard.

Gravitational wave memory refers to the permanent strain alteration left by strong events, such as merging compact objects. We demonstrate that this phenomenon can produce a stochastic background detectable by future observatories like LISA. This finding is significant because, unlike standard mergers, memory events occur exclusively at high redshifts, thereby dominating the signal in the distant cosmic past. We quantify the contribution of this component to the GW background and analyze its dependence on the merger rate, source masses, and duration. Our results indicate that memory from future LISA-detected events could dominate the overall signal at redshifts exceeding z=2.

We investigate a supersymmetry (SUSY)-breaking first-order phase transition occurring at the energy scale of $T \sim 10$ PeV. This transition generates a stochastic gravitational wave background detectable by future space-based interferometers. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this same scale can account for the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe via the decay of out-of-equilibrium SUSY leptons. The SUSY spectrum is engineered to remain consistent with current LHC constraints, while the SUSY-breaking scale aligns with the scale of supersymmetry breaking. Additionally, the energy scale of this transition facilitates the formation of primordial black holes.

Semantic communication aims to transmit the essential meanings of source data rather than raw bits, thereby enhancing spectral efficiency. This paper introduces a neuro-symbolic causal reasoning framework designed to jointly optimize semantic extraction, symbol allocation, and reconstruction within a signaling game environment. The signaling transceiver employs probabilistic neural networks to model signaling behaviors and a neuro-symbolic causal reasoning engine to deduce causal relationships from received signals for accurate target recovery. On the receiver side, a neuro-symbolic planner constructs a world model based on input data, utilizes a causal graph to infer cause-and-effect structures, and a symbolic classifier maps these relationships to appropriate action selections. The proposed system was evaluated against conventional signaling and standard semantic communication methods using the CIFAR-10 dataset and the Drosophila fly image set; results demonstrate significant performance gains in both spectral efficiency and reconstruction quality.

Word prediction is a fundamental task in Natural Language Processing (NLP) that involves suggesting the next word based on a preceding sequence. This study introduces a new approach combining the Naive Bayes algorithm with latent variable modeling to enhance performance. We evaluate our method against the standard Naive Bayes algorithm using the widely adopted benchmark dataset from the Stanford 3rd-party Corpora (SST-3) for the Word Prediction task. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed hybrid model achieves a 10% improvement in F1-score compared to the traditional Naive Bayes algorithm.

Recent session-based recommendation models have achieved significant success by leveraging attention mechanisms to capture user context within individual sessions. Nevertheless, these models typically treat every item as equally important, ignoring the inherent rank of candidates, and often fail to provide recommendations across multiple future sessions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes Two-Stage Ranking Candidate Embeddings (TSRE), a two-stage framework designed to enhance both recommendation accuracy and diversity. TSRE first employs a popular off-the-shelf ranking model to filter items, retaining only high-confidence items for subsequent processing. Subsequently, it constructs ranking-aware candidate embeddings for these retained items to refine the final recommendations. Extensive experiments conducted on three public datasets demonstrate that TSRE surpasses state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and diversity metrics. The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/zhengzizhou/TSRE.

We investigate the behavior of active colloids, such as self-propelled spheres, that move within activity gradients. This research focuses on systems containing "molecules," which are dimers formed by two spheres linked by a spring. We demonstrate that these structures can act as physical sensors for activity gradients, with their extension and internal vibration amplitude depending on the strength of the gradient. We further show that, in a homogeneous environment, these molecules behave like a heat engine, converting internal fluctuations into mechanical work. Consequently, in activity gradients, they function as external work engines, converting spatial variations in activity into both mechanical work and physical expansion. We analyze how these devices can perform work to lift a load and find that their efficiency surpasses that of standard Brownian ratchets, which rely solely on thermal fluctuations. Finally, we outline potential future research directions in this field.

Discrete fracture network (DFN) models are essential for simulating subsurface flow and transport, particularly in fractured reservoirs and for enhancing geologic carbon storage. This study introduces a novel mesh generation approach for creating DFN models, utilizing a conforming multi-dimensional structure that aligns with fracture and matrix interfaces. We solve the governing equations for flow and solute transport using the Mimetic Finite Difference (MFD) method, which ensures conservation across the entire domain, including the fractures themselves. Because the DFN model is inherently sparse, we apply a matrix reordering technique to optimize the sparsity of the system matrices, thereby accelerating the solution process. We validate our MFD-based simulations against analytical solutions for flow and solute transport, as well as established MFD results from a previous study that treated fractures as one-dimensional entities. Furthermore, we compare our proposed method to the Finite Volume Method (FVM). The findings demonstrate that the new mesh generation strategy combined with MFD offers a highly accurate and efficient framework for flow and solute transport simulations within DFN models.

This study addresses the challenges of collision avoidance and formation maintenance for a swarm of drones. It introduces a novel formation strategy grounded in point-set registration, wherein drones maintain formation by tracking designated reference points. This approach offers two primary advantages: it enables the use of established, efficient formation designs and ensures that the resulting drone cluster mirrors the original shape, size, and relative positions. The second method, optimized to $O(n)$, estimates distances based on drone velocities and their positions within the cellular grid. Both methods were evaluated through simulations involving formations of up to 100 drones. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively maintains formation integrity and prevents collisions, even when individual drones experience communication failures.

This study addresses an original problem in stochastic control involving stochastic functional differential delay equations (SDDEs) driven by fractional Brownian motion (FBM) with a Hurst parameter exceeding 0.5. Due to the lack of Markov properties in FBM, we adopt a mean-field framework to formulate the problem, assuming the dynamics depend only on the first moment of the distributed delays. This study introduces a two-parameter family of explicitly defined, finite-band Jaroshik-Zakharov potentials for the non-Hermitian Dirac operator, which interpolates between the elliptic and trigonometric cases. For every value of the parameter, these potentials enable the construction of a Dirac operator possessing a purely real spectrum.

This study introduces a two-tier heterogeneous Vehicular Ad-hoc Network (VANET) architecture designed to enhance communication coverage and reliability. The proposed system comprises an infrastructure tier consisting of Roadside Units (RSUs) and a vehicle-centric tier formed by Vehicle Relays (VRs). The objective is to maximize the average data transmission rate between Road Side Units and Onboard Units (OBU) by optimally positioning VRs. To achieve this, the paper develops a comprehensive analytical framework for characterizing the spatial distribution of VRs and OBUs, as well as modeling the one-dimensional and two-dimensional distances separating them. Furthermore, the authors derive the average transmission rate and outage probability within the system. The analytical results are validated through numerical simulations.

Although Wikipedia is renowned for its high editorial standards, it occasionally hosts articles of poor quality. While various initiatives exist to identify and rectify such content, this study introduces a novel, unsupervised approach that detects problematic pages by analyzing the inherent patterns in user editing activities. The methodology employs supervised machine learning to classify edits as either constructive or destructive, subsequently applying unsupervised techniques to the edit histories of articles exhibiting a predominance of harmful contributions. The results, which were validated through extensive human evaluations, demonstrate an article-level classification accuracy of 80.2%. Furthermore, this system successfully identified previously unknown issues in 39.1% of articles previously flagged by Wikipedia's quality assessment system.

Knowledge distillation offers a method for training smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a larger teacher, yet the prevalent techniques currently depend on access to a white-box teacher and its training data. This paper introduces a decision-based zero-shot knowledge distillation approach that circumvents the need for white-box access or training data for the teacher model. By employing an ensemble of decision-based metrics to quantify similarity between a teacher and a student, we facilitate knowledge transfer. We validate our methodology through experiments on image classification tasks, where the teacher consists of a deep neural network trained on the CIFAR-100 dataset, and the student is a decision tree. The results demonstrate that the student achieves a 10.5% accuracy improvement over standard training on CIFAR-100 via our approach, surpassing the accuracy of a baseline decision tree trained with CIFAR-100 by a margin of 10.5 percentage points.

This study extends the definition of topological T-duality to include duality pairs involving T-dualities on topological twisted tori with torus action. Imitation learning is a well-established method for enabling robots to acquire complex behaviors from expert demonstrations. However, a significant limitation exists: these demonstrations are often labor-intensive to create and difficult to modify. To overcome this, we introduce a novel approach called "co-imitation learning." This method enables a robot to master a task by collaborating directly with a human partner, effectively turning the human into the expert through the joint execution of the task. We demonstrate that this technique is task-agnostic, requiring no prior knowledge of the activity, and we validate its efficacy across various scenarios, including physical manipulation, virtual environments, and speech recognition.

We introduce a new dataset and corresponding model designed to track and reconstruct both hands and the objects they manipulate in real-world videos. This dataset features 1,100 sequences captured in natural environments, with ground-tright annotations for both hand and 3D object poses. To facilitate the tracking and reconstruction of these multiple moving parts, we developed a novel architecture that integrates a sequence-to-sequence approach with a set of pose-specific detectors. Specifically, we utilize an object detector to track each hand independently across frames, then feed these tracks into a sequence model that predicts the 3D orientation of the object. We evaluate our method against various baselines, including those using synthetic data, and achieve state-of-the-art performance on our benchmark. The complete dataset and source code are publicly available at https://hori-ogawa.github.io/hand-object-dataset/.

This work examines a class of noncrystallographic C-groups of rank 4 and interlacing number 2. These groups are defined by specific relations of type $(m_i, m_{i+1}) = (4,4)$ for all $i$ not equal to the central index, with the exception at index 2 following a pattern of $(m_1, 4, 4, m_4)$ where only $m_1$ and $m_4$ vary. We establish that these groups are distinct whenever $m_1 \neq m_4$. By analyzing the associated Coxeter diagrams, we identify two structural configurations: a linear chain diagram and a star-shaped (forked) diagram. For each case, we derive the corresponding group by specifying the variable orders $m_1$ and $m_4$ within type $(s, t) = (m_1, m_4)$ relations. Our findings demonstrate that these groups exhibit a high degree of symmetry, with every element conjugate to a standard reflection. Furthermore, we construct a representative coset graph for each group and determine their geometric properties, including the dimension and structure of the underlying geometry.

This paper introduces a novel, markerless method for performing robot extrinsic calibration using a depth camera and enhancing the associated 3D end-effector pose estimation. The core concept involves training a regression model to predict the robot's depth-captured features, which subsequently enables the inference of the robot's depth camera extrinsic parameters and end-effector pose from real-world scenes. We validate this approach using the Microsoft Azure Kinect, demonstrating its efficacy with both genuine and synthetic data. Furthermore, we provide an open-source implementation of the methodology at the following link: https://github.com/azadsh/robotcalib.

This study introduces a treatment interference framework wherein a unit's response to a treatment is determined by the proportion of neighboring units receiving that specific treatment within a fixed radius. We propose a method to identify the smallest K value that yields a statistically significant interference effect. Our findings indicate that, under our assumptions, Lasso regression provides an unbiased estimator of the treatment effect on units experiencing interference.

We investigate neutrino production mechanisms within the early phases of supernova explosions, focusing on reactions involving dark matter (DM) particles that annihilate via the exchange of pseudoscalar mediators. Our calculations reveal that neutrino luminosities can increase by several orders of magnitude compared to standard rates, a result driven by the presence of lepton asymmetry in the primordial neutrino distribution. This enhanced energy output significantly shortens the duration of the neutrino emission phase in the proto-neutron star environment. Consequently, this rapid cooling imposes stringent constraints on the parameters governing the interaction between DM and neutrons.

The Kronecker-Weyl equidistribution theorem establishes that the sequence $\{\alpha n + \beta n^2 \mid n \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is dense in the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ provided that $\alpha$ and $1$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\alpha$ is irrational. This paper presents a generalization to higher dimensions, proving the $k$-adic Kronecker-Weyl theorem: for any dimension $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the sequence $\{\alpha n + \beta n^2 \mid n \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is dense in $\mathbb{T}^k$ whenever the real components of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\alpha$ is irrational. Additionally, we demonstrate the metric independence of such vectors for almost all $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with respect to Lebesgue measure. These findings are derived from an analysis of Diophantine approximation involving polynomials with real coefficients, specifically the count of integer points $n$ within a given range $[1, N]$ that yield fractional parts close to a specified target vector.

We demonstrate that local complete intersection $k$-rational singularities exhibit the $k$-Du Bois property, with its $k$-Du Bois MSym complex exhibiting exactness outside the singular locus. Additionally, we prove that pointwise Gorenstein local rings are $k$-regular.

The Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) phase, a rare example of long-range order existing without a corresponding symmetry breaking, has historically been observed only in two-dimensional superfluids and XY magnets. This study reports the observation of the BKT phase in the Heisenberg magnet Cs₂CuCl₃, a material where magnetic spins are aligned perpendicular to an applied magnetic field. By employing neutron scattering to monitor the spin excitation spectrum, we demonstrated that the BKT phase can emerge in a Heisenberg system by suppressing the component of spin order parallel to the field, thereby reducing the effective dimensionality of the remaining spin degrees of freedom to one.

We propose a dark matter model where the relic abundance is split between an eV-scale sterile neutrino and an ultra-light axion. In this framework, the sterile neutrino forms via the resonant mechanism involving the decay of $Z$-bosons into $s$-wave $\nu_s$ and an Higgs boson. This process is mediated by an eV-scale scalar that couples to both the Higgs and $\nu_s$, and its production rate is subsequently suppressed by axion-photon interactions. We examine how the relic density of the resulting ultra-light axion varies with respect to the scalar's mass and coupling strength to the sterile neutrino.

Recent advances have established tighter limits on the computational complexity of magic states, though our work further refines these bounds for key single-qubit states. Specifically, we demonstrate that the T-state has a stabilizer rank of at most 2 (previously unknown), the T†-state requires a rank no greater than 3, and the Tℏ-state has a rank bounded by 5. These findings directly enhance the precision of near-term resource estimates for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

This study examines a spatially flat Friedmann-Robertson-Walker (FRW) universe incorporating Tsallis holographic dark energy within a complex-form quintessence model. We analyze the resulting dynamics of matter and dark energy, focusing on the equation of state parameter to determine conditions for the phantom divide. Furthermore, we investigate the evolution of energy density and the critical boundary separating quintessence and phantom quintessence regimes. Finally, we derive the critical value for the model parameter $\xi$ that marks the transition between these two quintessence types.

Pseudo-random number generators (PRNGs) are essential across numerous embedded systems, yet their generated sequences face criticism for lacking true randomness and being vulnerable to exploitation by malicious actors. This study introduces TuRaN, a novel true random number generator (TRNG) designed to extract entropy from SRAMs. TuRAN achieves this by applying supply voltage underscaling to SRAM cells, a technique that amplifies variations in cell switching times driven by process variations. The resulting data is processed through a post-processing pipeline comprising whitening and compression to guarantee output randomness and unpredictability. The research validates TuRAN's efficacy by demonstrating its successful operation on a commercial 65nm CMOS test chip and a fabricated 32nm CMOS SRAM array, both of which produced high-quality random numbers even at minimal underscaling levels.

This study introduces a nonvolatile resistive switching architecture based on a single molecular junction. We utilize a DFT/NEGF framework to examine the electronic characteristics of junctions featuring benzene-1,4-diamine junctions connected to gold electrodes with varying linker lengths. Our simulations reveal that junctions at a 1.2 nm gap operate as single-electron devices, functioning as resistance-based memory units where the state is dictated by the parity of electrons on the central molecule. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the binary information stored in this molecular system can be read out via a single-electron tunneling mechanism.

We establish a causal representation for mass-finite multi-loop scalar Feynman integrands, featuring logarithms of light-cone separations squared between massless propagators. This formulation enables the efficient numerical computation of these advanced integrals using standard techniques designed for simpler, lower-loop analogs.

This work presents a 1D 2-state quantum walk model on infinite lattice $\mathbb{Z}$ that mirrors the mathematical structure of Hermitian 1-D two-state non-unitary walks studied in previous research. We establish a unitary equivalence between this system and a Hermitian, time-dependent Schrödinger equation on half-line $[0,\infty)$ featuring boundary conditions at the boundary. Leveraging this connection, we derive a formula for the resolvent of the non-unitary walk's transition operator in terms of the eigenfunctions of its boundary parameter-dependent boundary matrix. Finally, we prove the completeness relation for these functions using a formula for the boundary matrix's spectral measure.

This study examines hybrid stars, which consist of quark matter alongside nuclear matter, utilizing the MIT bag model, Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model, and the Sigma-Omega-Rho model. The analysis focuses on the effects of the critical temperature and the speed of sound within the hybrid star structure. The study's findings indicate that quark deconfinement leads to a reduction in the maximum mass of hybrid stars. Additionally, the radius of the star is observed to decrease as the speed of sound within the quark core increases. The study concludes that the MIT bag model provides a superior fit to the observational data from the NICER mission compared to the NJL model.

This study examines a fast and slow light system involving a q-deformed two-level atom interacting with a mechanical membrane, where the deformation parameter is governed by the mechanical displacement. Employing the q-deformed su(2) algebra, we derive the system's Hamiltonian under the rotating wave approximation and apply first-order perturbation theory to analyze its optical response. Our results demonstrate that transparency windows, along with regions of fast and slow light, emerge within a completely incoherent environment. We further investigate the impacts of q-deformation on these phenomena, revealing that the deformation parameter significantly influences the positions and magnitudes of peaks associated with anomalous dispersion, as well as the strength of the resulting transparencies, group velocity delays, and enhancement factors. Specifically, we observe that increasing the deformation parameter shifts the anom dispersion regions, leading to corresponding movements in the transparency windows and areas of fast/slow light; simultaneously, the maximum values for group velocity enhancement and transparency intensity rise, whereas the peak group delay diminishes.

The two-body rotational framework, known as the two-body or two-rotor model, has been employed to investigate negative-parity states in $^{16}$O, a nucleus characterized by a single nucleon outside a closed $sd$-shell. This model successfully accounts for the observed energy levels and the collective features of the $2^-$ states. In this work, we introduce a rotational two-rotor model specifically designed for a nucleus comprising a closed $sd$-shell plus one nucleon, aiming to explore the emergence of scissors modes under conditions of negative R-parity.

This study examines the spin and orbital fluctuations in doped transition metal oxide films, specifically focusing on the effects of dimensionality and strain. We present a comprehensive framework for analyzing the spin susceptibility of a $d$-electron system, which incorporates both crystal field and spin-orbit coupling effects. We demonstrate that in the absence of an external magnetic field, the spin susceptibility of a non-Kramers doublet exhibits a maximum at a finite temperature, whereas it follows a Curie law for Kramers degenerate states. We propose that this Curie-law deviation arises from orbital fluctuations and can be observed in ultrathin oxide films where electrons are confined to two dimensions and occupy orbital doublets. We further illustrate how strain can shift the susceptibility peak to lower temperatures and enhance its magnitude. Additionally, we explore the impact of electron-electron interactions and orbital fluctuations on the specific heat and magnetic specific heat. Our findings indicate that interactions can produce a Schottky-like anomaly in the temperature dependence of the specific heat. Finally, we discuss the physical origins of these phenomena and their experimental observability.

We introduce a new framework for laser-cozing atoms within dissipative optical lattices, a system that functions as an open quantum entity. By integrating rate equations with a stochastically switching two-level quantum model, we demonstrate that the momentum distribution of a single atom can be regulated with high precision. Furthermore, we reveal a novel anomalous stochastic behavior in the position of an atom, characterized by a fractional Brownian motion with a tunable Hurst exponent. This anomaly stems from the non-Markovian nature of the effective dynamics governing the single particle. Leveraging this statistical anomaly, we have designed a quantum measurement protocol that surpasses the standard quantum limit, achieving superior precision in determining atomic positions.

This study examines the interdependencies within the cryptocurrency trading network, focusing on 20 major cryptocurrencies traded on the Kraken exchange. We construct a cryptocurrency trading network (CTN) where each cryptocurrency represents a node, and links reflect the trading pairs between them. By analyzing the structure of this network, we observe that its topology remains consistent regardless of the time scale. Furthermore, we evaluate the return spillover effects among these assets using a high-order dependency framework. Our findings indicate that the relationships between cryptocurrencies are not merely pairwise; rather, they involve significant high-order interactions, underscoring the necessity of incorporating such dynamics into financial modeling.

This study employs path integral molecular dynamics (PIMD) simulations to examine the effects of nuclear quantum effects (NQEs) on the structural and dynamical characteristics of sulfuric acid-water clusters, denoted as $(H_2SO_4)(H_2O)_n$ for $n=1$ to $5$. The simulations were conducted at 200 K, a temperature relevant to atmospheric conditions, utilizing a polarizable force field. The results indicate that NQEs significantly enhance the mobility of protons and oxygens while simultaneously reducing the zero-point energy contributions to structural stability. Specifically, the analysis of the mean squared displacement reveals that NQEs accelerate sulfur and acid-water oxygen diffusion, whereas the diffusion rate for hydroxyl and water protons/oxygens is already substantial even in the absence of these effects. Structurally, NQEs weaken intramolecular bonds within the sulfuric acid moiety but leave intermolecular hydrogen bonding largely unaffected. The study concludes that while NQEs are a critical factor in the dynamics of such clusters, their impact on overall structure remains negligible.

Furthermore, we demonstrate that this topological space is itself compact.

Furthermore, we show how the $\lambda$ norm and the $\lambda$ norm of a function with a Weyl fractional part of order $k$ are related to this complexity. We also demonstrate that the $\lambda$ norm of a function with a Weyl fractional part of order $k$ is related to the approximation error of smooth functions with Weyl fractional part of order $k$. Finally, we show that the $\lambda$ norm of a function with a Weyl fractional part of order $k$ is related to the approximation error of smooth functions with Weyl fractional part of order $k$.

We outline a method for directly extracting the Wilson coefficients of the effective operators governing $B^0\to K^{*0}\mu^+\mu^-$ decays by analyzing angular distributions across the entire $q^2$ spectrum. This approach offers significant benefits over the standard practice of determining coefficients from averaged differential decay rates, specifically by circumventing the need for theoretical models of the hadronic form factors. We present the angular distributions' functional form and the corresponding likelihood, which can be evaluated numerically once experimental data are obtained. Furthermore, we examine the sensitivity of this extraction strategy to various sources of systematic uncertainty.

Automated essay scoring (AES) represents a significant challenge in machine translation and is frequently evaluated through the Buil Automatic Essay Scoring (BAES) task. This study introduces a novel approach to AES by employing pre-trained transformer models, specifically BERT, to generate numerical ratings for test samples. Our methodology involves data augmentation to create a robust training set comprising 100,000 examples derived from the original 10,000 entries of the BAES corpus. By leveraging this augmented dataset, our model achieved a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.8022 on the 2018 test set, surpassing the performance of submissions from the previous two years in the same competition.

We introduce a novel class of multivariate distributions defined by marginal independence structures. For a random vector $\mathbf{X} = (X_1, \dots, X_d)$, this category encompasses all marginal distributions of the form $P_{\mathbf{X} \setminus X_i}$ for each $i \in \{1, \dots, d\}$. This framework generalizes elliptical distributions and extends the concept of marginal homogeneity. We demonstrate that these models correspond to a specific subset of orthant-dependent distributions and derive properties regarding their modes, moments, and rank correlations. Additionally, we establish the existence of a stochastic representation $\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{Y} \odot \mathbf{U}$, where $\mathbf{Y}$ represents a vector of independent positive random variables and $\mathbf{U}$ a vector of independent sign variables. Finally, we examine the application of these models to binary data and discuss their utility in analyzing causal effects within binary treatment and outcome scenarios.

This paper introduces a dynamic framework for mobility that allocates advancement chances based on individual effort and innate talent. We demonstrate that when advancement relies solely on effort, a rigid system produces higher long-term dynamism than a flexible one, whereas systems in which advancement depends on both effort and talent exhibit greater flexibility than rigid structures. Conversely, under conditions where advancement is purely determined by talent, a flexible system surpasses a rigid one in generating higher dynamism. We also examine how long-term dynamism responds to variations in the parameters governing advancement allocation.

This paper introduces a modified RingCT framework designed to enhance privacy by enabling the inclusion of multiple transactions within a single, broader CT transaction. We term this approach "Delegated RingCT" (DRRingCT). In this model, a single signature validates the entire group, effectively acting as if those multiple transactions were signed by a unified signer. This structure offers two primary advantages: first, it shields the identities of the actual senders for grouped transactions, and second, it reduces blockspace consumption by allowing multiple transfers to occupy just one transaction record. We have implemented this proposal on the Cardano network and provide empirical data demonstrating its practicality.

We introduce a framework for analyzing the difficulty of addressing specific subclasses of linear systems, derived from Fitch, Koutis, and Litsyn's (2019) work on sparsity-structured systems. This approach utilizes the concept of space complexity to evaluate hardness, establishing that systems corresponding to planar graphs are complete under this reduction. We further demonstrate that many significant system types fall within this hard category, including those governed by finite difference discretizations of elliptic partial differential equations and models based on undirected graphical models. Consequently, solving these systems necessitates memory resources scaling linearly with the number of variables. This conclusion holds even when the bandwidth of the coefficient matrix is sublinear relative to the total variable count.

This study reports the initial observation of $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} =$ 13 TeV yielding three massive gauge bosons, with an integrated luminosity of 13.3 fb$^{-1}$ collected by the CMS detector at the LHC. The analysis examines the decay channels $eee$, $e\mu\mu$, $e\mu e\mu$, and $\mu e\mu e\mu$, where the final leptons are identified as electrons or muons. This study introduces an enhanced Hebrew Universal Dependencies (Hebrew-UD) treebank, constructed by domain adaptation techniques. We evaluate the efficacy of this approach through cross-domain parsing tests, comparing the adapted model against one trained exclusively on domain-specific data. The findings indicate that while the adapted model underperforms relative to a system trained on target-domain data, it achieves sufficient accuracy for practical application.
