The paper introduces a novel, collaborative data-driven modeling methodology for multi-variable systems, where multiple groups independently construct local models using distinct sets of process variables. These individual models are subsequently integrated via a coalition of co-associating variable pairs to form a single unified system-wide model. The core of this approach lies in an iterative algorithm that iteratively identifies and links variables between groups until convergence is achieved. The method's validity is substantiated through theoretical proofs demonstrating model consistency and the algorithm's convergence. Furthermore, a specific data-collation strategy is proposed to enhance the resulting unified model's accuracy. The efficacy of this framework is verified through simulations on a multi-tank system, with additional application demonstrated in the cooperative data-driven modeling of two distinct groups analyzing the Tennessee Eastman benchmark process variables.

This study examines the performance of a specific class of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, known as degree-correlated correlated-regular (DC-RC) codes, on the binary erasure channel. These codes feature a fixed, uniform distribution of bit-node and check-node degrees within each specified group, subject to constraints regarding the variance of degree distributions across groups. We introduce an ensemble of DC-RC codes defined by node count, degree values, and designated degree-correlation parameters for each node group. By deriving a degree-degree correlation matrix for group $g$, we establish a corresponding matrix of coupling coefficients that dictates the probability of specific degree pairings between nodes in that group. Leveraging a density evolution (DE) framework, we compute the average conditional degree profiles for bit and check nodes in group $g$ relative to the group's bit-node degree distribution. These results are visualized through a two-dimensional plot of average versus actual node degree. We further identify optimal coupling coefficients for each group to maximize the minimum erasure decoding threshold. Numerical evaluations confirm that proposed DC-RC ensembles can surpass the thresholds of standard regular LDPC codes with uniform random degree distributions.

Although system-level robustness verification is essential for autonomous systems, ensuring safety remains difficult in general control scenarios. This paper introduces a novel predictive safety filter that leverages system-level synthesis (SLY) techniques to guarantee safety. The proposed solution transforms an arbitrary control task into a specific form amenable to straightforward safety assurance. Implementation-wise, the safety filter operates by solving a finite-horizon optimal control problem at each time step, utilizing the original cost function. By restricting the control inputs to a pre-identified safe subset, the system ensures constraint compliance over a forecast window. The "safe control set" is determined through a system-level approach, where robustness constraints are converted into convex conditions applicable to a specific class of linear Gaussian systems. The study also presents a method to extend this control set for broader applicability and demonstrates the approach's efficacy in ensuring the safe navigation of unmanned aerial vehicles.

Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) offers unconditional security assurance, a capability enhanced by the decoy-state method, which counters weaknesses inherent in single-photon sources. Despite these security guarantees, standard QKD with decoy states remains susceptible to various measurement-side attacks, as demonstrated by the 2010 work of Yuan et al., who showed that an adversary can manipulate detectors to extract full information about the quantum states while remaining undetected. Building on this, we introduce a novel attack strategy that requires less precise control over the photon phase compared to the original Yuan et al. method. This "hack" successfully compromises a commercial QKD system operating at distances exceeding 100 kilometers. Our findings underscore the necessity of rigorous security audits for all components within the QKD apparatus, particularly the detection modules.

Although pretraining corpora are widely regarded as the primary factor shaping a language model's capabilities, their specific impact on in-context learning (ICL) remains poorly understood. This study investigates how different pretraining datasets influence the performance of a 1.7-billion parameter model across various ICL tasks. Our findings reveal a significant correlation between corpus composition and ICI success: data rich in mathematical expressions enhances performance on arithmetic tasks, while exposure to code improves the execution of programming code. Furthermore, we observe that the model's proficiency in specific tasks depends on the presence of corresponding syntactic structures during pretraining. These insights offer valuable guidance for future corpus engineering aimed at optimizing a model's task-specific ICI performance.

We utilize the ENZO cosmological hydrodynamical simulation to investigate the radiative cooling and fragmentation of hot intracluster medium (ICM) clouds, focusing on how cloud properties like mass, radius, and density evolve over time. Our analysis examines the influence of radiative cooling, magnetic fields, and thermal conduction on cloud evolution. We define the cooling time relative to the free-fall time to characterize cooling efficiency, demonstrating that this ratio serves as a robust proxy for cloud size and mass. We observe that in the absence of these external factors, cloud cooling proceeds rapidly, leading to significant growth and shattering. Conversely, when thermal conduction or magnetic fields are present, cloud evolution is markedly altered. Specifically, anisotropic thermal conduction can suppress cloud growth and shattering, whereas magnetic fields tend to enhance cloud expansion and increase the cooling time.

This review examines CP violation within the Standard Model concerning beauty and charm quarks, with a specific emphasis on meson systems such as $B^0_d$, $B^0_s$, and $B_c^\pm$, as well as the $B^\pm$ and $D^\pm$ dublets. It provides an overview of current experimental findings and theoretical predictions, with a summary of key results from the LHCb collaboration, complemented by an outlook on future prospects.

We investigate the high-energy scattering of transverse-traceless bosonic strings within the framework of superstring theory. By analyzing the high-energy limits of the scattering amplitudes for various string states, we derive novel hard scattering expressions. Furthermore, we propose an extended Gross conjecture that encompasses the scattering amplitudes of all string states, including those previously unaccounted for.

The advent of 5G introduces a new generation of wireless networks designed to support diverse use cases, ranging from massive machine-type communications and enhanced mobile broadband to ultra-reliable low-latency services. To meet the stringent demands of data volume, latency, and energy efficiency, 5G architectures rely heavily on network slicing and automation. This paper examines the core management procedures for self-organized sustainable networks, analyzing their critical role in enabling a flexible, efficient, and reliable 5G infrastructure.

Zero-shot Text-to-Speech (TTS) is a rapidly advancing field within speech synthesis, with current state-of-the-art methods primarily relying on large-scale, unconstrained speech datasets. This study introduces a zero-resource TTS framework that utilizes transcripts generated from perceptual acoustic units. We propose a transcript generation system that maps acoustic features to a vocabulary of phonemes, utilizing a phoneme set smaller than conventional consonant-vowel frameworks. This system is trained using only the acoustic labels provided by existing supervised phone alignment tools. We demonstrate that using these perceptual acoustic phonemes yields superior results compared to standard unconstrained phoneme sets, particularly in systems employing unsupervised speech representation learning.

Motion planning is a critical challenge in robotics, and this paper introduces a multi-stage approach to address it. We begin by outlining a general framework for creating multi-stage plans and demonstrate its application to a two-stage problem involving a planar robot with degrees of freedom. A key component of this system is an algorithm that generates a sequence of coupled convex problems, utilizing data-driven relaxations based on McCormen envelopes to approximate the robot's collision avoidance constraints. We evaluate the planning performance of this method across three distinct environments, comparing the resulting plans against those produced by standard planning algorithms.

We establish new bounds on the transformation of quantum states under completely positive trace-preserving maps, with a specific focus on how probabilistic quantum state conversion is constrained. Our findings are derived from a broader set of limits governing the conversion of quantum resources, applied here to states representing coherence and purity. Notably, these bounds significantly enhance existing knowledge regarding the conversion of pure coherent states into other pure coherent states.

While drinking coffee from a cup, the liquid's sloshing can cause spills. We demonstrate that this motion resembles a nonlinear pendulum driven by an external pump, where the "links" correspond to the air-liquid and liquid-cup interfaces. By employing the method of averaging, we derive an effective pendulum model that captures the coexisting stable equilibrium points and separatrices, alongside the periodic oscillations known as "sloshing modes." These modes are defined by periods that are integer multiples of the cup's shaking frequency. Furthermore, we identify regions of quasi-periodic motion termed "chaos layers," which may lead to significant oscillation amplitudes. The resulting amplitude depends on the specific parameters of the driving force, the cup, and the coffee itself.

Decentralized learning (DL) offers a scalable approach for multi-agent systems, enabling agents to collaboratively train a model using only local data and limited communication with neighbors. However, standard DL often yields poor performance when applied to real-world scenarios due to data heterogeneity among agents. This paper introduces DR-DSGD, a novel robust DL algorithm designed to mitigate the impact of statistical shifts in local data distributions. By integrating robust optimization principles, the method ensures a stable training outcome despite potential distributional variations. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's convergence properties, establishing that it reaches a stationary point of the robust optimization problem with a sublinear rate. Furthermore, numerical experiments confirm that DR-DSGD outperforms existing methods in environments characterized by heterogeneous data distributions.

We introduce a novel method for modeling the early-time evolution in relativistic nuclei-nuclei collisions by employing hydrodynamic attractors. This approach bypasses the need to solve the equations of motion for the anisotropic rapidity evolution of the system. Our findings indicate that this technique offers an efficient means of determining the initial energy density and analyzing particle multiplicity generation.

This study investigates the origins of outflows surrounding forming stars, specifically examining whether high-velocity jets from protostars can clear a path for broader, slower material. We employed 3D smoothed-particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations to model the ejection of high-velocity jets from a central source moving at 10% of the speed of light ($c$). Our results indicate that these jets effectively carve out a low-density channel in the surrounding envelope, facilitating the subsequent outflow of larger volumes of matter along this trajectory. We further analyzed the momentum transfer between jets and the ambient medium, demonstrating that the total momentum of the resulting wide-angle, low-velocity outflow can surpass that of the jets themselves. These findings suggest a viable mechanism for generating wide-angle outflows and offer a potential explanation for the frequently observed coexistence of both high and low-velocity outflows in young stellar objects.

This study introduces a balanced control approach for constrained nonlinear systems, aiming to achieve an equilibrium between achieving desired control objectives and adhering to system limitations. This framework is applicable to a broad class of nonlinear systems featuring both state and control limitations, utilizing model predictive control (MPC) as its methodology. To ensure constraint satisfaction, the proposed scheme employs a terminal set derived from a linear feedback law grounded in a restricted invariant set. Furthermore, it offers a balanced performance by dynamically adjusting the weighting on control inputs within the MPC cost function based on the magnitude of available control authority. The analysis demonstrates that this control strategy guarantees recursive feasibility and ensures a stable closed-loop behavior with a specific degree of asymptotic stability. The practicality and advantages of this methodology are illustrated through simulation results applied to two systems: one featuring an academic example and another representing a wind turbine.

This study presents a new analytical approach to the perturbative motion of Solar System bodies, incorporating Solar Radiation Pressure (SRP) alongside the first-order effects of the Poynting-Robertson (PR) drag. By utilizing a simplified Hamiltonian derived from the Laskar et al. (1993) model, we determine the equilibrium states of SRP-driven semi-secular resonances. These equilibrium values are subsequently validated through numerical simulations, which also assess the stability of these resonances and the magnitude of secular frequency shifts induced by the force. The findings indicate that SRP significantly alters the secular dynamics of small particles within the main asteroid belt, the Kuiper belt, and the Eris orbit. Specifically, the resonance locations and the associated frequency shifts are observed to vary with the particle's $\beta$-factor, a parameter quantifying the ratio of radiation pressure to solar gravity.

We introduce a first-principles tight-binding framework for describing light-matter interactions, grounded in a generalized, gauge-invariant gradient magnetic vector potential. This approach enables the construction of vector potential-dependent Hamiltonians by integrating magnetic effects into first-principles band structures. We demonstrate the gauge invariance of our method and validate its accuracy against established numerical benchmarks. Additionally, we showcase its utility by modeling the non-reciprocal transmission and circular photogalvanic effect in a honeycomb lattice.

This study introduces a novel 2D and 3D semantic object pose estimation framework designed for category-level object manipulation. We propose a new keypoint representation that encodes semantic properties of keypoints, enabling robust pose estimation even under significant semantic variations. Furthermore, we present a new optimal semantic correspondence method capable of handling semantic variations in object shapes and keypoints. Extensive experiments on the COCO dataset demonstrate that our approach surpasses current state-of-the-art methods in semantic object pose estimation.

This study introduces a novel confidence region for a Cauchy distribution based on a sample of $n$ independent and identically distributed observations. The resulting region is disk-shaped if the data are drawn from a 2D Cauchy model and box- or square-shaped for a 3D model. The method generalizes the robust M-estimation framework for location parameters, achieving the highest possible confidence level by optimizing the location estimate. The shape of the region is governed by a single tuning parameter, which controls the confidence level; this relationship is detailed in a straightforward lookup table. The approach remains resilient against outliers and produces highly symmetric intervals for individual data points. Furthermore, the method is straightforward to implement in standard statistical software.

Basket trials are increasingly utilized in oncology to evaluate single agents across multiple tumor types, aiming to identify responsive subgroups. This approach is particularly advantageous for rare diseases lacking sufficient patient volumes per subgroup for individualized analysis. Nevertheless, determining the requisite sample size for such trials presents a complex challenge. This study introduces a Bayesian framework to ascertain sample size requirements for basket trials that leverage data borrowing among subsets. By employing a hierarchical logistic regression model, we illustrate how to calculate samples based on desired power for each subgroup, while simultaneously accounting for information sharing. Furthermore, we propose a method to calculate a unified sample size that ensures predetermined power levels for all subgroups.

This paper introduces a novel control architecture termed Sequential Loop Closing (SLC), designed to integrate the benefits of both single-loop closing (SLC) and multi-loop closing approaches. The primary advantage of SLC lies in its capability to address internal model principles without necessitating an explicit internal model definition. While the original SLC method has been evaluated on high-precision platforms, this study extends its application to mechatronic systems governed by a nonlinear dynamic model, specifically within a motion control context. To achieve linear parameter variations (LPV) suitable for SLC implementation, the nonlinear model undergoes linearization through a scheduling variable. The variable is selected to ensure a direct correlation with the system's operating range, thereby facilitating the construction of an appropriate internal model. This model is subsequently embedded within the SLC framework to enhance tracking performance. The proposed methodology is validated through experiments on a physical high-precision linear stage, demonstrating superior tracking accuracy compared to conventional multi-loop closing techniques.

This paper introduces PRNet, a novel deep learning framework designed for the registration of partial point clouds. Unlike existing deep learning methods for rigid registration that typically depend on complete input data or require pre-existing ground-truth annotations, PRNet operates effectively on incomplete "partial-to-partial" data and demands no training labels. By utilizing two self-supervised loss functions, the system enforces feature extraction consistency and feature alignment, thereby enabling high-quality training without external ground truth. Additionally, the method incorporates a novel descriptor capable of handling significant variations in the amount of overlap between point clouds. Training is conducted exclusively on the ModelNet40 dataset, yet the approach demonstrates robust performance when tested on the more challenging ShapeNet Part benchmark. The codebase is publicly available at https://github.com/zhengzheng1999/PRNet.

A group exhibits the property $R_\infty$ when the count of conjugacy classes within its rational cover is infinite considers the $n$-th Baumslag-Solair group, $B_{T}$, which is defined by the relations $a^{-1}b^tb=b$. This paper demonstrates that for every nilpotent quotient of the group $B_{T}$, the property $R_\infty$ holds. This result extends previous findings by Kim and Kwon, who showed the property holds for the original group and its abelian subgroups, to an even broader class.

The Standard Model predicts a vacuum instability that occurs if the Higgs boson mass exceeds approximately $125$ GeV and top quark mass falls below roughly $172$ GeV. While the measured Higgs mass aligns with this threshold, current experimental uncertainties regarding the top quark mass allow for a metastable electroweak vacuum, implying that any new physics must manifest before this instability decays the universe. This study investigates the capabilities of various proposed colliders to detect this instability, specifically analyzing how precisely each could determine the Higgs–top coupling, which governs the decay rate. We demonstrate that a $100$ TeV proton collider could constrain this coupling to a $1\%$ precision, thereby extending the stability boundary of the electroweak vacuum by an additional order of magnitude in terms of energy scale.

We introduce a trajectory-basis robust inversion technique for time-resolved scattering experiments. This approach represents the time-evolving wavefunction as a superposition of a compact set of pre-optimized trajectories, which are computed prior to the inversion process using a forward propagation step. Subsequently, a backward propagation step updates the wavefunction coefficients to fit the experimental time-resolved yied data. We demonstrate the application of this method to a one-dimensional model of a conical intersection, showing that it achieves high reconstruction accuracy for a variety of samples while maintaining computational efficiency.

This study calculates the light-cone distribution amplitudes for $D^*$ and $D^*_s$ mesons, employing the model of Bethe-Salpeter wave functions. The results demonstrate that the leading twist components, $ \phi_1^{V}(x) $ and $ \phi_1^{A}(x) $, exhibit a significant dependence on the scale, whereas the higher-twist contributions, $ \phi_2^{V}(x) $ and $ \phi_2^{A}(x) $, remain largely invariant under scale changes. The study further determines the corresponding moments up to order $n=8$.

This work establishes the Fourier-based definitions of the $\mathcal{FS}^{\{1,\gamma\}}$ and $\mathcal{FS}^{\{1,\gamma}\}$ non-trivial Hermite functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ for parameters $0<\gamma\leq 1$. We demonstrate that the associated Toeplitz operators are normal if and only if the underlying functions vanish identically.

Accurate instance segmentation is crucial for advancing medical image analysis, yet current methods predominantly focus on well-annotated standard imaging modalities. In contrast, research into annotating and training models for unlabeled or emerging modalities remains scarce. This study introduces an innovative approach utilizing segmentation CycleGANs to transfer instance-level labels from known modalities to new, target modalities without requiring additional annotation efforts. Evaluated across three datasets for brain and liver instance segmentation, the results demonstrate that this method successfully segments instances in both established and newly introduced modalities. Furthermore, the proposed technique enables the creation of segmentation models for new modalities with significantly reduced annotation costs.

This study introduces a novel end-to-end action anticipation framework that integrates an RNN with the recurrent gate mechanism, alongside a kernelized feature learning approach utilizing Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernels. The proposed system is designed to forecast upcoming movements based on a sequential input of skeletal features. By employing kernelized feature extraction with RBF kernels, the model achieves superior generalization when tested on unseen actions and subjects. Furthermore, the incorporation of the recurrent gate enhances the network's capacity to retain critical long-term dependencies within the sequence. Experimental evaluations conducted on the standard dataset, NTU-60, demonstrate that this method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy.

On April 12, 1985, the M4.5 dwarf star AD Leonis experienced a superflare that was exceptionally bright in the near-ultraviolet (NUV) spectrum. This event allowed for the first-ever modeling of the flare's continuum emission, revealing that the chromosphere was heated to temperatures of approximately 10,000 K, with the NUV radiation originating from the lower photosphere at around 5,000 K. The modeled spectral energy distribution aligns well with the observed data, indicating that the flare's energy release occurred within the photosphere. This finding suggests that the magnetic reconnection responsible for the flare took place deep within the stellar atmosphere, rather than solely in the upper chromosphere or corona.

We examine the deformation of $\mathrm{G}_2$-instantons within the nearly $\mathrm{G}_2$ framework. Our findings demonstrate that the deformation spaces of these instantons are smooth manifolds, with their dimensions restricted to specific discrete values.

This paper investigates $C$-normal weighted composition operators within the space $T_{\psi,\phi}^n(C)$ acting on $H^2$ and identifies specific sufficient conditions under which such an operator exhibits $C$-normality.

We present an algorithm that constructs the bijection between $t$-core $p'$-partitions of $n$ and partitions of $n$ whose $p$-power dividing order is $t$. This bijection is generated using a walk on the additive residue graph, where the walk's length corresponds to a specific large partition defined by its $p$-core. We further establish an $[p]$-adic formulation of the Freudenthal-Rook rule and demonstrate how this approach generalizes the traditional Freudenthal-Rook rule.

Point cloud models have recently emerged as a significant advancement in 3D vision, offering superior geometric fidelity and semantic precision compared to traditional surface models. However, existing 3D data augmentation strategies for these models remain underdeveloped. This paper introduces Transformed Point Cloud (TPC), a novel, generalizable framework designed specifically for transforming point cloud models. TPC operates by applying random transformations to the vertices of these models, which are subsequently optimized using an end-to-end learning approach to ensure semantic and geometric consistency. To achieve this, the method utilizes three key components: a consistency decoder, a reconstruction loss function, and a smoothing regularizer. Empirical results demonstrate that TPC effectively enhances the representation capabilities of point cloud models for semantic understanding and geometric reasoning tasks. The code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/zhengzheng1999/Point-Cloud-Transformation-Control.

This study examines medium access control (MAC) protocols within FMCW radar networks, specifically evaluating slotted ALOHA and a novel version of CSMA. The primary objective is to analyze the performance of these protocols in preventing interference between radar signals, ultimately deriving the throughput for slotted ALOHA and determining the optimal access slot duration to maximize this throughput. Additionally, the paper introduces a new MAC protocol based on CSMA, analyzes its performance, and compares the results with standard slotted ALOHA.

This study examines the influence of Entangled Two-Photon Absorption (ETPA) within an optical medium placed at one arm of a Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interferometer. We demonstrate that when the probe and signal photons from the HOM source possess identical spectral profiles, ETPA results in a symmetric reduction of the characteristic HOM dip depth. Conversely, if a spectral mismatch exists between the two entangled photons, the ETPA-induced modification becomes spectrally dependent. In such cases, the original symmetric dip distorts into an asymmetric shape, with the specific form of this asymmetry dictated by the degree of spectral disparity between the probe and signal modes.

This paper investigates circle-equivariant elliptic cohomology within the framework of vector space representations $V$ over complex fields. The study establishes a general method to compute values for all such spaces $V$ and subsequently derives explicit formulas applicable to homogeneous spaces where the circle group acts as the maximal compact subgroup of a complex semisimple Lie group $G$.

Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning (TKGR) aims to forecast missing facts within a knowledge graph by integrating temporal information. Although embedding-based approaches have proven effective for TKGR, most existing models rely on complex, task-specific structures and often fail to leverage established embedding methods. This paper introduces a simple yet efficient framework that achieves high performance in TKGR by combining the benefits of pre-existing embeddings with two parameter-optimized components: a model-independent relation embedding and a specific entity-observation projector designed for dimensionality reduction. This projector enables the creation of compact joint representations for entities and temporal data, allowing the approach to reach state-of-the-art accuracy on benchmark datasets while remaining flexible enough to adapt to various underlying embedding techniques.

While robotic grasping has been extensively studied, the influence of acoustic cues on how humans and robots acquire objects remains largely unexplored. This study investigates the role of ground sound in grasping, specifically examining its reliance on object properties like material and size, as well as spatial location. Results indicate that both object properties and placement significantly affect the ground sound, with human participants demonstrating the ability to accurately guess an object's identity based solely on these acoustic cues. Furthermore, we evaluated various simulation-based strategies for generating acoustic cues to guide a robotic hand, ultimately identifying a simulation policy capable of successfully acquiring a specific target object using ground sound.

This study introduces a hybrid quantum circuit designed to validate the Bell theorem without using inequalities in a scenario where both entanglement verification and the correlations required for the standard Bell inequality without inequalities are not perfect. We show that our proposed non-locality demonstration surpasses previous methods in resilience against experimental imperfections. Specifically, we successfully verified the Bell state and generated the necessary correlations to satisfy the criteria for a valid Bell inequality, even when the final output correlations are noisy. Our findings indicate that perfect quantum entanglement is not a strict prerequisite for this variant of the Bell theorem; rather, high-fidelity Bell-state preparation is the sole requirement.

Flat bands signify a rare scenario where the absence of thermal motion in a system is driven by quantum interference rather than disorder. In this study, we demonstrate that flat bands can emerge in a disordered environment by employing a dual mechanism: first, we identify flat bands within a disordered Huxley model that feature random hopping and reveal a corresponding Fermi surface in the flat band region. Second, we show that flat bands appear in a disordered Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, which possesses regular hopping but random site potentials. Furthermore, we investigate the conditions under which flat bands coexist with extended states. Our findings indicate that flat bands can span an entire energy band, yet a system may still host extended states if the density of states remains finite at the band edges.

Hydrogen-rich hydrides are currently regarded as the most promising candidates for achieving room-temperature superconductivity, a state that could revolutionize energy storage and electrical transmission. This study utilizes density functional theory (DFT) to investigate hydrogen boride (H3BH6), a novel hydrogen-rich material, for its potential superconducting properties. Our calculations reveal that H3BH6 crystallizes in a monoclinic C2/m phase, exhibiting a predicted lattice constant of 4.80 Å. The material displays strong covalent bonding and a pronounced Fermi surface nesting effect, resulting in a high density of states at the Fermi level. Furthermore, the phonon dispersion analysis confirms the absence of soft modes, indicating dynamic stability. By employing the Allen-Dynes modified McMillan equation, we estimate a superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$) of 10.2 K using a Coulomb pseudopotential ($\mu^*$) of 0.1. These findings suggest that while H3BH6 is not a candidate for high-$T_c$ superconductivity, its structural and electronic characteristics offer a solid foundation for exploring future superconducting materials within the hydrogen-boron system.

This study examines the statistical properties of runs in flattened Young tableaux. Specifically, we derive closed-form expressions for the mean and variance, along with the second moment, of the run count across flattened partition tableaux of Young tableaus of shape $\lambda$ within the symmetric group $S_n$. Additionally, we establish the limiting distribution as $n$ approaches infinity and provide the corresponding mean and variance for this distribution.

This work examines amenability within arithmetic groups, specifically focusing on the concepts of charm and stiffness. A finitely generated discrete group is termed charming if every finitely generated subgroup possesses finite index; such groups are stiff when every finitely presented co-finitely presented. The study establishes stiffness for certain arithmetic groups of rank two and proves that all congruence subgroups of semisimple simply connected linear algebraic groups defined over Q are both charming and stiff. Additionally, the paper addresses the long-standing question regarding the existence of infinitely many non-isomorphic charming families of such groups. The authors demonstrate the existence of infinitely many distinct families among semisimple simply connected linear algebraic groups of rank 2 equipped with structures of varying Q-structures.

This paper presents the formal validation of a fail-operational driving management system used in automotive applications. The described architecture employs a dual microcontroller setup operating in a compare-and-fail mode to ensure safety-critical functions. The investigation begins by detailing the system's operational framework and its corresponding safety requirements, followed by the introduction of a functional model implemented within an automaton. This mathematical representation is subsequently utilized to demonstrate the formal verification process, which confirms that the designed control logic adheres strictly to its defined safety specifications.

This study introduces a novel, data-centric approach to clustering dynamical systems, which is particularly suited for scenarios where system equations are unknown and only time-series observations are available. The methodology constructs a similarity matrix by estimating system-specific influences through time-reversed prediction errors, followed by clustering based on this matrix using the K-Means algorithm. The proposed framework was validated through simulations on the Duffing oscillator and various Chua circuits, as well as through testing on the Human Activity Dataset to demonstrate its efficacy in distinguishing distinct behaviors within partial observation contexts.

This paper examines Leibniz's foundational procedures for infinitesimal calculus, specifically focusing on the derivation of differentiation and integration rules, the resolution of differential equations, and the formulation of the fundamental theorem of calculus. We reconstruct these methods within three distinct conceptual frameworks: the substitution model, the limit model, and the continuous object model. By analyzing Leibniz's original techniques through these lenses, we demonstrate that the substitution model offers the most compelling explanation for his reasoning.

This study examines how foreground subtraction influences the power spectrum of neutral hydrogen intensity mapping. We demonstrate that foreground removal can introduce significant systematic errors, particularly when the foreground field exhibits a non-Gaussian distribution. To quantify this impact, we developed a novel analytical framework based on perturbation theory, which models the power spectrum of the cleaned data as a convolution of the foreground and target signals. This approach enables us to predict the residual contamination on the power spectrum resulting from foreground subtraction. We also evaluate the efficacy of various minimum variance estimators in mitigating these effects. Our results indicate that for future surveys, such as the proposed CHIME/SEAMLESS experiment, the power spectrum of the H I signal can be recovered with a fidelity exceeding 95% after cleaning.

In this work, we demonstrate that for any $d \geq 2$, the independence of $2d$ unital $*$-homomorphisms from $D_{+}^{d}$ into $C(S^{1})$ is guaranteed provided there exists a specific set of $2d$ operators meeting certain conditions. Additionally, we establish the equivalence between two statements: (i) the existence of $n$ independent unital $*$-homomorphisms from $D_{+}^{d}$ into any separable $C^{*}$-algebra containing $M_{k}$ for all $k$, whenever $n$ is sufficiently large relative to $d$, and (ii) the ability to construct $n$ operators $A_{1},\dots,A_{n}$ in $M_{k}$ that are locally asymptotically multiplicative and pairwise asymptotically angle-independent.

Hybrid recommender systems have emerged as a viable solution to mitigate inherent limitations found in both collaborative and content-based filtering approaches. This paper introduces a novel hybrid model that leverages document context alongside user historical actions to generate personalized suggestions. The proposed system constructs a matrix of documents within each user's profile, subsequently calculating document similarity to identify similar items. The final recommendation score integrates three key factors: the document similarity metric, the global popularity of items, and the frequency with which specific items have been interacted with by the user. Empirical evaluation using the MovieLens dataset demonstrates that this method outperforms standard collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, and existing hybrid techniques.

This paper examines two topics regarding random matrices within the framework of free probability. The first section investigates when a self-adjoint matrix $A$ and the shifted matrix $A+\lambda I$ are free, specifically analyzing the transition from being "not free" to "stably free" as the magnitude of $\lambda$ grows. The approach relies on the concept of freeness for operators on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, which is defined by the property that the operators generate a maximal abelian subalgebra within the full matrix algebra. The discussion then moves to the second section, which addresses conditional freeness. It is demonstrated that the adjacency matrices of two independent, uniformly chosen regular directed graphs on $n$ vertices, conditioned upon sharing a specific eigenvector, exhibit conditional freeness relative to the projection onto that eigenvector. This finding provides an alternative derivation for the eigenvalue distribution of adjacency matrices in $d$-regular directed graphs.

This study revisits the monitoring of real-time properties expressed in Timed Automata (TA) and Timed Scene Graphs (TSG). We establish an effective method for determining the satisfiability of a given TA within a trace, a task proven to be undecidable in general. Additionally, we introduce a framework for a specific subset of monitorable TAs characterized by deterministic structures and bounded clocks. For this subset, we define the concept of synchronized product—integrating a property defined by TAs with a property monitor. This approach enables the construction of a monitor for any timed property that can be expressed as a conjunction with a synchronized product of a monitorable TA. We also present a method to determine the monitorability of a given timed property, which is decidable. Finally, we define a specific class of timed properties that are guaranteed to be monitorable.

The $\bar{B}_s^0 \to J/\psi a_0(980)\bar{b}_0(980)$ decay offers a unique opportunity to investigate the nature of the mixed $a_0(980)-f_0(980)$ system. Utilizing data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 3 fb$^{-1}$ collected by the BESIII experiment at the $\sqrt{s}=4.6$ GeCm energy, we report the first observation of this decay. The branching fraction is determined to be $\mathcal{B}(\bar{B}_s^0 \to J/\psi a_0(980)\bar{b}_0(980)) = (1.44^{+0.48}_{-0.42})\% \otimes (0.03^{+0.01}_{-0.01}) \otimes (0.01^{+0.01}_{-0.01}) \otimes (0.01^{+0.01}_{-0.01}) \otimes (0.01^{+0.01}_{-0.01}) \otimes (0.01^{+0.01}_{-0.01}) \otimes (0.01^{+0.01}_{-0.01

The GRAVITY acquisition camera (AC) is a dedicated device designed to precisely align four infrared beam combiners within the VLTI/Interferometer. It operates at wavelengths spanning 1.25 to 1.65 µm, utilizing a dual-mode design that supports both single-pointing and wide-field capabilities. This camera is essential for enabling GRAVITY's high-precision astrometry and its ability to image extended sources. This paper details the AC's technical specifications, operational performance, and in-field testing outcomes.

This study examines the performance of algorithms for the generalized $k$-center problem on metric spaces characterized by low doubling dimension or highway dimension. We establish that instances defined by doubling dimension exhibit a quasi-polynomial approximation ratio, whereas the subclass defined by highway dimension admits only an exponential approximation ratio. These findings are supported by lower bounds derived from the local connectivity of a problem instance's optimal solution.

In this paper, we establish several new theorems regarding the linear independence of $e^Q(z)$, $e^Q(z-\eta)$, and $(z-\zop)^m$ within the framework of complex analysis. Additionally, we derive some findings on the linear independence of $e^Q(z)$, $e^Q(z-\eta)$, and $e^P(z-\zop)$ for $Q(z)$, $P(z)$ polynomials and $\eta$, $\zop$ non-zero complex constants. These findings are employed to enhance several existing results on the uniqueness of entire functions when compared with their shifts.

This study addresses the problem of determining the rank and a basis for the null space of a given matrix $A$ with entries in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, subject to a relative error margin. We introduce two new algorithms that achieve this task using fewer evaluations of the input polynomial compared to existing methods. The first algorithm runs in expected time $O(M(n)^{1+o(1)})$ and the second in $O(M(n)^{2+o(1)})$, where $n$ denotes the matrix's dimension and $M(n)$ represents the cost of multiplying two $n \times n$ matrices. Additionally, we present an accelerated variant of the $O(M(n)^{2+o(1)})$ algorithm capable of halting prematurely to yield an exact rank and null space basis for specific matrices.

In quantum optics, the standard approach to generating parity-correlated photon pairs involves spontaneous four-wave mixing (SFWM) within optical fibers. This process produces two modes, each containing a single photon, where the presence of one guarantees the other. This paper introduces a novel extension of SFWM that yields balanced pair emissions confined to just one mode, yet maintains parity symmetry between even and odd total photon numbers. Uniquely, this high-parity correlation is safeguarded by a conserved parity operator, allowing the resulting states to surpass the classical limit known as the anti-bunching inequality.

This study introduces a new analytical model for the structure of alkali metals, which are characterized by complex electron-electron interactions. We derive a simple, accurate, and precise analytical expression for the compressibility of these systems, which is essential for calculating the equation of state. We demonstrate that the derived equation of state for lithium plasma aligns closely with established data for this highly non-ideal system. Furthermore, we provide a novel, simple, and precise method to determine the ionization degree of alkali metals, which is critical for modeling astrophysical phenomena.

This study examines the vector meson spectrum within a medium exhibiting chiral imbalance, a scenario induced by fermions in vacuum. Utilizing the formalism of the Holographic Light Front Quark Model, the analysis incorporates the impact of both the medium's chiral imbalance and transverse momentum. The results indicate that the values of the medium's chiral chemical potential and the mesons' spin significantly influence the vector mesons' masses.

This study addresses the fundamental task of estimating the size of an unknown network where nodes communicate via message passing. We investigate a scenario in which a fraction of nodes are Byzantine—malicious actors capable of sending arbitrary data to their neighbors. Our primary goal is to design an estimator that remains accurate despite these faults, even when Byzantine nodes attempt to deceive regular nodes about the network's true scale. We present a novel, simple, and decentralized protocol that enables honest nodes to estimate the total network size with high precision. We prove that this method achieves the best possible accuracy given current constraints and that its requirements for honesty are minimal. Our findings indicate that the fundamental limit for size estimation scales as $\tilde{O}(f/n)$, where $n$ represents the total number of nodes and $f$ is the count of Byzantine nodes.

Numerical relativity simulations of binary black hole mergers typically employ the 3+1 decomposition of Einstein's equations, splitting them into evolution equations and spatial constraints. While constraint-violating solutions exist, they are expected to decay over time; thus, standard practice involves periodically re-satisfying the constraints through methods like constraint damping or full constraint damping. This study introduces a novel approach: a constraint projection algorithm that fully restores both the momentum and Hamiltonian constraints at every time step. We demonstrate that this new method is stable and conserves momentum, with results from numerical tests on perturbed Schwarzschild and binary black hole systems showing that it reduces constraint violations to levels orders of magnitude lower than those achieved by standard evolution techniques.

The design of the JUNO neutrino experiment relies on utilizing 20-inch photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) to detect the anticipated slow scintillation light produced by electron antineutrino inverse beta decays. To ensure a uniform response across the array, JUNO requires approximately 76,000 fully assembled and optically equipped PMTs, with specifications demanding a relative wavelength-dependent photocathode efficiency variation of no more than 3% across the 400–550 nm range. This paper outlines the mass testing and characterization procedures performed on the bare PMTs. These activities encompassed evaluating dark current, gain, and photocathode efficiency for every tube, with the latter determined using a dedicated, wavelength-tunable LED light source.

Predicting future values in multidimensional time series is a critical challenge across numerous fields, including economics, engineering, and healthcare. While existing methods often rely on statistical models or deep learning approaches, they typically fail to capture the temporal dependencies inherent in the data. This study introduces a novel Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (AGCN) designed to address multidimensional time series forecasting. The proposed framework constructs a dynamic graph structure to model temporal relationships and employs an adaptive learning strategy to optimize convolutional parameters. Experimental evaluations on real-world datasets demonstrate that AGCN consistently outperforms current state-ofthe-art methods.

This study presents the analysis of atmospheric dispersion (AD) data collected by the 2.5-meter Isaac Newton Telescope (INT) at La Palma, Canary Islands. The primary aim is to evaluate the performance of various AD models against actual observations. The measured datasets were gathered using the instrument's built-in AD compensator, which functions as a variable, axially symmetric prism. The analysis indicates that the observed AD follows a well-behaved, rotationally symmetric pattern that aligns closely with a power law. The study further assesses the suitability of power laws, Cauchy functions, and an elliptical formulation in modeling the dispersion. The results demonstrate that a power law offers the most accurate fit to the data, achieving a reduced chi-squared value of 1.02.

Pre-trained language models (PLMs) have achieved remarkable success across numerous NLP tasks, largely due to their capacity to absorb diverse linguistic patterns through knowledge distillation. However, current methods are constrained by the single-teacher framework, which limits the volume and variety of information imparted, and by the computational expense of ensemble approaches that stack multiple teachers. This paper introduces Pairwise Iterative Logits Ensemble (PILE), a novel, computationally efficient distillation strategy that iteratively enhances an individual pre-trained model. PILE constructs knowledge ensembles by pairing the target student with multiple data augmentation variants of itself, effectively distilling from "self" across various augmented states. By integrating these iterative pairwise interactions, PILE significantly boosts both the linguistic proficiency and reasoning capabilities of the student. Empirical evaluations across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that PILE surpasses existing techniques, delivering superior performance at a fraction of the cost.

This study introduces a novel intensity interferometry approach designed to identify signatures of ultralight bosonic dark matter. The proposed method relies on measuring correlated fluctuations in intensity that arise when two laser beams interact with a mutually coherent classical field, potentially within an experiment utilizing a dual-laser interferometer.

This study examines the uniqueness of L1-minimization in the continuum, a problem with relevance to tomographic imaging. We establish a criterion for unique basis pursuit by formulating it as the requirement that a specific measure be strictly positive on a particular class of test functions. Our analysis demonstrates that this criterion holds for the Landau systems of both discrete and continuous types, as well as for the Shepp-Young filter applied to continuous systems.

The P4 language has become a standard for defining programmable, match-action table-based switches with flexible capabilities. Although the original P4-1.6 compiler front-end is publicly available, its backend remains closed-source, restricting the ability of researchers and developers to adapt the tool for novel hardware architectures. This paper introduces an open-source P4-1.6 compiler backend tailored for reconfigurable switch architectures featuring match-tables. The implementation supports various reconfiguration strategies, including one, two, and three-dimensional mapping approaches. Additionally, the authors present experimental data evaluating the runtime performance of the generated programs across different reconfiguration methods.

This study examines the vector transport equation on unstructured 2D and 3D meshes using Raviart-RT1 elements, a common choice for incompressible flow simulations. The analysis reveals that the standard vectorization of the curl operator combined with the conventional $\mathbb{P}_1$ integration rule results in a discretization error of $O(h^2)$. To enhance this accuracy, the paper introduces two improved approaches: (1) employing a higher-order ($\mathbb{P}_2$) rule for face flux integration, and (2) adopting a new formula for computing face normal vectors. The latter method leverages shape function derivatives and face area coordinates to determine face normals by averaging across all vertices. Numerical experiments confirm that the first improvement yields second-order accuracy ($\mathbb{O}(h^2)$), whereas the proposed normal vector strategy achieves third-order accuracy ($\mathbb{O}(h^3)$).

Federized learning has become a prominent privacy-preserving framework for machine learning, enabling model training on distributed data without centralizing it. However, the standard federated approach often results in performance biases, where the global model favors users with large contributions, thereby reducing accuracy for clients with smaller local data. To address this, researchers have introduced fairness-enhancing techniques, yet these solutions often compromise privacy by exposing sensitive information about the amount of data each client holds. In response, this study proposes integrating differential privacy into federated learning to ensure that a user's data volume remains confidential. Our solution, called FairDP, delivers a differentially private model trained in a manner that is equitable across all distributed participants. Unlike current approaches, Fairp does not require knowledge of the size of each user's local dataset. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that our method offers robust privacy protections against data volume inference while maintaining competitive predictive performance.

This paper details the discovery of an excited $B_c^+$ state by the LHCb collaboration, achieved through a search for its decay into $J/\psi\pi^+\pi^-\pi^-$ at the hadron beauty collider operating at center-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s}=8\text{ TeV}$. Utilizing data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $3\text{ fb}^{-1}$, the analysis identifies the state with a statistical significance exceeding $5\sigma$. The observed mass is $6.891 \pm 0.012\text{ (stat)} \pm 0.010\text{ (syst)}\,\text{GeV}/c^2$, with a width of $0.054 \pm 0.012\text{ (stat)} \pm 0.010\text{ (syst)}\,\text{MeV}$. The newly identified resonance is consistent with a $2P$ $1^-$ $B_c^+$ meson.

This paper proposes a novel numerical method for solving first-order systems of ordinary differential equations using a continuous Runge-Kutta approach. We construct this scheme based on $s$ abscissae and derive its order conditions by employing Taylor series expansions alongside those involving partial Bell polynomials. A convergence analysis is performed, establishing that for any order $p$, there exist methods utilizing $s=p+1$ collocation points. Furthermore, we examine the algebraic order conditions for achieving $Q(p,p)$ convergence and demonstrate the applicability of this framework to certain delay differential equations.

Model-parallel deep learning has emerged as a viable solution for training large-scale neural networks, yet it face significant challenges due to extensive communication overhead and intricate communication patterns. To address these issues, we introduce Model-parallel Learning with Critic (MoLC), a novel framework that employs local critics to enhance communication efficiency. By enabling the partitioning of both computation and communication tasks across multiple nodes, MoLC leverages local critics to optimize this partitioning. Our experimental results demonstrate that this approach reduces total training time by up to 2.5 times compared to traditional model-parallel strategies.

This study examines chaotic scattering within the dissipative Hénon-Heiley three-dimensional (3D) system, specifically investigating the fractal boundaries separating the basins of attraction. We demonstrate that introducing weak dissipation induces a transition marked by a substantial increase in the fractal dimension of these boundary surfaces. Additionally, we show that for the 1:1 and 1:-1 resonances, the fraction of the boundary surface exhibiting a local dimension of 3 is significantly larger under dissipative conditions compared to the conservative case. These findings are substantiated by both numerical simulations and theoretical analysis.

We present an accidental mechanism that can extend the lifetime of light $Z'$ bosons, which typically induce rare processes such as neutral meson mixing. These bosons can exist at mass levels reaching tens of GeV, a scale typically inaccessible to current experiments, provided they couple to third-generation fermions. This mechanism operates by confining the decay products of the $Z'$ within a dense environment, such as the interior of a compact star, thereby sequestering the interaction energy and suppressing observable effects in terrestrial laboratories.

Recognizing human actions within videos is a fundamental challenge in computer vision. While existing methods often rely on hand-crafted features or 3D convolutions, this paper introduces a novel hierarchical attention network designed for action recognition. This method leverages pre-trained image networks to extract frame-level features, which are then organized into spatial-temporal segments. To capture both local and global information across these segments, the model employs a dual mechanism: segment-level attention highlights significant areas, while poolable attention aggregates information hierarchically. Experiments conducted on two standard datasets, UCF101 and HMDB51, demonstrate that this hierarchical attention network achieves state-of-the-art performance.

This study investigates the dynamics of scalar particles interacting with Reissner-Nordström anti-de Sitter (RNdS) black holes, specifically examining charge capture, mass increment, and alterations in the specific angular momentum of the holes. By analyzing these effects, the work establishes the conditions under which such particles can be absorbed, confirming that the process respects charge conservation and cosmic censorship. Furthermore, the reaction of the horizon to particle capture is examined, with calculations of temperature and entropy changes during the event. The research also explores the validity of the first and second laws of thermodynamics in this context, concluding that they hold true. Finally, the document assesses the weak cosmic censorship conjecture for the resulting extremal RNdS black holes, determining whether it remains valid after particle capture.
This piece offers a brief overview of the process by which stars form.

We present a technique for calculating various entropy metrics using the Nested Sampling algorithm, a method originally devised for Bayesian model comparison. This approach is particularly effective when dealing with high-dimensional entropies, a scenario where conventional methods often fail. We evaluate our method against two standard alternatives using data from the LIGO-Virgo collaboration concerning gravitational waves from binary black hole mergers.

This paper investigates a nonlinear hyperbolic conservation law, $[1]$ presents a solution concept based on measure-valued Kruzkov entropy solutions, and proves the existence of such solutions via an approximation method employing regularized entropy conditions. Additionally, a uniqueness result is derived under a boundedness constraint on the initial data, measured using the Bourgain-Brué-Diallo-Robert variant of the bounded variation norm.

This study introduces NB coded, a novel classification framework designed to detect network attacks on devices with constrained resources. The system relies on a two-stage architecture: an encoder that compresses input data into a compact feature set, followed by a Naive Bayes classifier. This approach optimizes the processing of the reduced feature set, enabling efficient attack identification. The framework was evaluated using the NSL-KDD dataset, demonstrating 99.2% accuracy. Furthermore, the model's efficiency was validated on an embedded system, the Raspberry Pi, confirming its practical applicability for resource-restricted environments.

This work examines the growth behavior of word maps within groups that contain a polycyclic normal subgroup. As a specific application, we demonstrate that the growth of the center in a finitely generated solvable group is either linear or superlinear, thereby excluding the possibility of exactly quadratic growth.

This study introduces a computational framework designed to identify biological locomotion in video footage. The methodology relies on a specific gait signature, defined as a periodic oscillation in the vertical position of the center of mass, which occurs when an organism moves its center of mass forward on a horizontal plane while maintaining a constant forward velocity. The proposed system operates in two phases: first, it estimates the three-dimensional positions of a subject's joints from two-dimensional video data using a biomechanical model of human movement; second, it calculates the center of mass trajectory to verify the presence of the target signature. The primary objective is to leverage this unique signaure for applications in privacy-protecting anonymous video analytics. Experimental results indicate that the framework achieves a detection accuracy of 85% for general locomotion and 80% specifically for walking.

Optimizing power networks is vital for ensuring reliable electricity delivery, a challenge that can be addressed through quantum algorithms. This study introduces a hybrid framework integrating quantum and classical methods to resolve network reconfiguration and optimal power dispatch issues. We detail the proposed workflow and demonstrate its efficacy using a 33-bus test system, supported by results from both simulated quantum execution and actual hardware runs on real devices.

A primary objective of theoretical physics is to identify the fundamental laws governing nature, a process that typically involves constructing mathematical models based on a limited set of basic principles and then validating these models through experimental or observational data. This work presents a data-driven methodology for uncovering such underlying physical laws by leveraging the universality of polynomial chaos expansions. We demonstrate the approach's efficacy in analyzing three distinct scenarios: a Brownian motion system, a fluid dynamics model, and a system exhibiting chaotic behavior. Furthermore, the framework is applied to a dataset concerning the solar wind, showcasing its ability to simultaneously derive physical relationships and detect inconsistencies within the data.

This study presents a search for pair-produced, long-lived, massive charged particles with masses exceeding 1 TeV, utilizing data from the ATLAS detector at the LHC, which corresponds to 36 fb$^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity collected from proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV. The analysis targets particles that deposit significant energy, characterized by a specific ionisation loss of $dE/dx > 2.5~\text{MeV cm}^{-2}$ within the tracker. The results are compared against Monte Carlo simulations of the Standard Model background, revealing no statistically significant excess. The study establishes exclusion limits at 95% confidence level, excluding particle masses in the range of 1.02–1.08 TeV for a pair-production cross-section of 1 fb, and 1.0–1.08 TeV for 10 fb. The specific model-dependent limits for heavy neutralinos and staus from supersymmetry are determined to be 1.02 TeV and 1.08 TeV, respectively.

We present a theoretical and experimental demonstration achieving a 97% on-chelp single-photon collection efficiency, utilizing a quantum dot integrated within a ridge semiconductor waveguide. This result surpasses previous achievements in semiconductor chip-based single-photon emitters and is comparable to the highest efficiencies found in cavity-coupled systems. We attribute this high performance to the waveguide's large optical mode confinement near the quantum dot, which enables efficient light extraction. These findings establish a new performance benchmark for future quantum networks and computing systems.

The boson peak represents a prominent feature in the scattering intensity observed in amorphous materials at low frequencies, a phenomenon widely regarded as a signature of excess low-frequency vibrations in disordered systems. This study examines the boson peak in protiated and deuterated poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) using neutron scattering techniques. By applying a Lorentzian fit to the frequency-dependent imaginary part of the dynamic structure factor, $S(Q,\omega)$, we observe that the bos peak shifts toward higher frequencies as temperature decreases. Additionally, the peak's maximum position varies with the hydrogen-to-deuterium ratio in the samples. These findings are interpreted through a model wherein the boson peak arises from an inhomogeneous distribution of potential energy surfaces, reflecting diverse local environments within the material.

This work examines the numerical evaluation of multi-loop, multi-scale Feynman integrals, which are essential for bridging experimental observations with theoretical predictions in high-energy physics. We concentrate on integrals that generate branch-cut singularities, noting that these can be resolved using a combination of standard techniques and methods derived from symbolical algorithms. This approach enables high-precision evaluations suitable for physical applications.

We establish a set of sum rules that determine the normalized integrals of eigenchannels for absorbed and reflected energies in scattering systems. These relations enable the determination of energy deposition normalization constants for the first eigenchannel without requiring detailed knowledge of the underlying eigenchannel functions. Furthermore, these formulas reveal a connection between the normalization of the first deposition eigenchannel and the scattering matrix, as well as the scattering polarizability.

The Far Infrared (FIR) emission from the Far 3-kpc Arm, a known interstellar arm, is detected at 21 cm, revealing a complex network of HI filaments. These filaments are organized into two primary structures: a southern component situated at approximately -10° declination and a northern one near -5° declination. The southern structure is continuous and extends from l = 280° to l = 340°, while the northern one spans from l = 280° to l = 350°. The study analyzes HI absorption against background sources to determine the arm's physical parameters. The Far 3-kpc Arm is located at a distance of 6.5 ± 0.5 kpc, with a mean radial velocity of -100 ± 1 km s⁻¹, a mean HI column density of 1.6 × 10²¹ cm⁻², and a mean mass surface density of 0.6 M☉ pc⁻². The arm's width is estimated at 1.2 ± 0.2 kpc, and its inclination angle is 60° ± 5°. The galactocentric distance is calculated to be 10.5 ± 1.5 kpc. The arm's position relative to the Perseus arm is defined by a galactocentric angle of 290° ±

Multi-objective optimization seeks a set of non-dominated solutions, known as the Pareto front, which offers various trade-offs among conflicting objectives. In practical applications, decision-makers often struggle to select a single final outcome due to the difficulty of weighing these differing goals against each other. Consequently, maintaining diversity on the Pareto front is critical, as it ensures that solution candidates exhibiting distinct characteristics remain available for consideration. This study evaluates the ability of ten state-of-the-art multi-objective evolutionary algorithms to generate diverse phenotypes within the population and concludes that increasing phenotypic diversity can be achieved by integrating a dedicated diversity maintenance mechanism.

This study examines the multilateral stable roommates problem in 3D, where each participant seeks a stable pairing consisting of two individuals, and preferences regarding these pairs are governed by three distinct, rank-based component preferences that can be summed. We establish the existence of at least one such stable configuration under these conditions. Furthermore, we introduce an efficient algorithm capable of generating a stable configuration from any quasi-transitive preference profile. Lastly, we analyze the problem's computational complexity by determining its parameterized complexity with respect to the count of incomparable pairs.

This study examines the influence of electron-phonon coupling on valley physics in two-dimensional systems. We demonstrate that in systems lacking inversion symmetry, this coupling induces a temperature-dependent shift in valley chemical potentials, a phenomenon that can be detected via an anomalous Hall effect. Additionally, we analyze systems with a sublattice symmetry breaking caused by staggered potentials, showing that electron-phonon interactions generate an elevated Kohn-Luttinger mass near valley points. This effect amplifies the impact of impurity scattering and can restore valley polarization even in the presence of valley-antisymmetric short-range disorder.

This work defines a cloud as a family of finite metric spaces that exhibits both scale and shape convergence as it approaches infinity. For any cloud, we establish that the associated cloud space—consisting of all such converging sequences within a fixed class—is complete under the induced Gromov-Hausdorff metric. Furthermore, we demonstrate that every cloud space possesses a center, defined as a specific metric space (also represented as an equivalence class) that minimizes the maximal distance to all elements in that space.

This paper introduces a millimeter-wave patch antenna featuring a ground plane with a cross-shaped slot, designed to achieve both wide bandwidth and an extensive angular coverage. Simulations and experiments confirm that the proposed antenna operates with a bandwidth of 10.2 GHz (spanning 23.1 to 33.3 GHz) and maintains a wide radiation pattern with stable gain across 0° to ±60° in both azimuth and elevation. To validate this broad angular performance, measurements were conducted using a standard horn antenna as a reference. Furthermore, the study demonstrates the feasibility of employing this antenna for wideband angle estimation through the analysis of its co-polarization and cross-polarization radiation patterns.

This paper introduces a decision framework for fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC) designed to determine the most probable logical bit and qubit operations based on received syndrome information. We demonstrate that this decoding challenge can be effectively addressed using reinforcement learning (RL). The proposed method employs a neural network to forecast logical operations, while an RL agent learns to optimize decoding performance through iterative training. We evaluated this approach on the surface code instances containing up to 1,000 faulty qubits. Results indicate that the agent achieves a success rate of 99.99% on a 23-by-23 lattice and 99.9% on a 77-by-77 lattice, even after being trained exclusively on problems of the smaller size.

Quantum metrology offers a pathway to surpass the limitations of classical measurement techniques, yet its practical application is often hinderled by the fragile nature of quantum states, which are susceptible to decoherence. This paper demonstrates that within a network of two cavities, one can achieve precise, rapid, and robust phase estimation by leveraging the cavity's specific jump metrology. By utilizing the unique features of the coupling-induced dark state, the proposed scheme allows for quantum phase estimation that proceeds at an enhanced rate while resisting environmental noise. Furthermore, we validate the effectiveness of our protocol through a noise-resilient quantum phase estimation experiment simulated via a quantum circuit on IBM's quantum hardware.

The PHENIX collaboration at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) presents its first measurement of direct photon-hadron correlations in Au+Au collisions, alongside results from d+Au and p+p systems. These datasets were collected at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV using a trigger that selected high-transverse-momentum direct photons ($p_{_{T}}>5$ GeV/$c$) within the central rapidity range ($|\eta|<0.35$). The correlated hadrons were analyzed across various azimuthal angles relative to the photons, with hadron transverse momentum bins extending up to $p_{_{T}}>25$ GeV/$c$. The observed suppression of high-$p_{_{T}}$ hadrons in the forward region is consistent with expectations from cold nuclear matter effects seen in d+Au collisions. Fermionic many-body systems represent a significant challenge for both classical and quantum technologies. In this work, we investigate the dynamics of spinless fermions on a 1D lattice featuring nearest-neighbor repulsion and hopping, as well as long-range repulsive interactions within the context of frustrated systems on a 2D square lattice. To model these scenarios, we employ the Kramers-Mannigoth (Keldysh) real-time framework, utilizing a quantum circuit composed of continuous-variable (CV) and qubit components. We propose a hybrid analog-digital model where Hamiltonian parameters are modulated continuously, contrasting this with standard discrete gate-based digital simulations. This hybrid strategy demonstrates superior efficiency in qubit utilization and gate complexity. Our results indicate that simulating fermionic dynamics with this hybrid digital-analog method offers a viable pathway for near-future quantum applications.

The 3D structured light (SLM) technique is an interferometrically based, non-invasive method for generating and measuring surface topographies, typically requiring the application of several patterns. However, achieving high precision in the presence of ambient light, vibration, or when measuring reflective tissues necessitates utilizing polarized structured light patterns. This study introduces a novel pattern generation algorithm that integrates a fuzzy logic controller (FLC) with a spatial light modulator (SLM). The proposed method employs an iterative approach to create structured light patterns capable of determining the phase of the reflected wave from a polarized beam, thereby enabling the reconstruction of 3D structures even under noisy conditions. The system's efficacy was validated through simulations and experimental trials on biological samples, including chicken eggs and chicken skin, demonstrating its ability to accurately map 3D surfaces of highly reflective tissues.

The device features a sensor thickness of 150 µm and collection electrodes with a 100 µm diameter and 200 µm spacing, fabricated on an aluminum nitride (AlN) substrate.
